parties:
Mukshed Ali Dafadar
Vs.
Alahibox Sardar and others
full_judgment:
Sikder Maqbul Huq, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties no. 1-4 to show cause as to why the impugned order no. 70 dated 2.5.91 passed in Misc. Case No. 160 of 1989 by the learned Assistant Judge Monirampur Upazilla, Jessore should not be set aside.

2. The petitioner Moksed Ali Dafadar and opposite party no. 8 Fuljan Bibi alias Fulmoti Bibi, as plaintiffs, filed Title Suit No. 125 of 1984 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Manirampur and obtained the decree in terms of solenama against some of the defendants and ex-parte against the rest.

3. Opposite party nos. 1-4 filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure hereinafter referred to as the Code for setting aside the ex-parte decree against them on the ground of non-service of summons etc. upon them and the said application was registered as Misc. Case No. 160 of 1989 and thereafter the Misc. Case was dismissed for default on 19.3.91 as the petitioner of the Misc. Case failed to appear before the court. The opposite parties no. 2 and 3 on 14.4.91 filed an application under section 151 of the Code for vacating the dismissal order alleging that they had no other alternative way to get the relief as prayed for and the learned Assistant Judge by his impugned order on 2.5.91 allowed the prayer and restored the Misc. Case to its original file and number.

4. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order the plaintiff petitioner has preferred this revisional application.

5. Mr. Md. Abdur Rahim, the learned Advocate appealing for the petitioner, submits that the petition under section 151 of the Code was not maintainable in view of the fact that the impugned order was appealable as per provision of Order 43 Rule 1 (d) of the Code. There is no denying of the fact that an order dismissing or rejecting an application under order 9 Rule 13 of the Code is appealable.

6. The learned Assistant Judge in his impugned order has referred to illustration 33 at page 328 of the Code of Civil Procedure by Mullah not mentioning the Edition of the book. Be that as it may, it appears that in Mulla's Code of Civil Procedure Vol. 1, 13th Edition (1981) published by the Law Publishing Company, Lahore (Pakistan) at page 902 under Synopsis -5 Illustration: (page 898): when inherent powers exercised, it has been mentioned in illustration 34 that although the Code contains no express provisions on the matter, the Court has inherent power to restore an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code which had been dismissed for default. The learned Assistant Judge did not mention a single word about the merit of the application in his judgment.

<u>7. It is now a well settled principle of law that under certain circumstances an order rejecting or dismissing for default a Misc. Case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code can be set aside or vacated. The learned advocate appearing for the petitioner in support of his argument has referred to the case of Abdul Majid Talukder Vs. Abdur Rob Talukdar reported in 32 DLR, (1981) page 57 and also to the case of Abdul Kader Chowdhury Vs. Nurul Islam and others reported in 43 DLR (AD) page 128. It has been held in the last mentioned reported case that the defendant petitioner having a remedy by way of appeal under Order 43, Rule 1 (d) of the Code could not maintain the application under section 151 thereof for setting aside an order of dismissal of a Misc. Case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code and such an application is barred under all circumstances. In the said reported case the application for setting aside of the dismissal order was filed after 7 days of the dismissal order for default of the Misc. case. It was further held that the filing of an application after such delay is also not tenable. It has also been held in the case reported in 32 DLR (1980) page 57 that section 151 of the Code has no application in which relief is obtainable by way of appeal from dismissal of an application filed under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code but, where the default is due to the mistake of the officer of the court or of the court itself, the aggrieved person may avail of the provisions of section 151 of the Code for rectification of such mistake and that the court itself may rectify its mistake in appropriate cases under its inherent powers.</u>

8. The impugned order was not passed due to the fault of any officer of the court or of the court itself and there appears no extra-ordinary circumstances bringing the application of the petitioner within the ambit of the provisions of section 151 of the Code.

9. Thus it is apparent that the application under section 151 of the Code for setting aside the dismissal order was misconceived and not maintainable and the petitioners of the Misc. Case had proper relief by way of appeal under Order 43 Rule 1(b) of the Code. Therefore it is crystal clear that the learned Assistant Judge committed an error of law resulting in error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned order. I find merit in the Rule.

10. In the result the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

11. Communicate the order to the court below at once.

End.

parties:
Abdul Haque J and another 
Vs. 
Shone Ali @ Moulana Shamsul Haque & ors.
full_judgment:
Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, J:- This Rule under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure was issued at the instance of plaintiffs as petitioners, directing the defendant opposite parties to show cause why the judgment and decree dated 14.7.1992 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Patuakhali in Title Appeal No. 144 of 1991 reversing these dated 24.9.1991 dated 24.9.1991 passed by the Assistant Judge, Galachipa, Patuakhali in Title Suit No. 81 of 1985 dated 24.9.1991 passed by the Assistant Judge, Galachipa, Patuakhali in Title Suit No. 81 of 1985 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Short facts, necessary for the purpose of this Rule is that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 81 of 1985 before the Assistant Judge, Galachipa, Patuakhali impleading the opposite parties as defendants seeking a decree for declaration of their title in the suit land stating, inter-alia, that the land appertaining to C.S. Khatian Nos. 17,217,218, of Mouja Chhaila Bunia of Police-Station-Galachipa originally belonged to Araj Ali to the extent of one third share, who having been in possession and enjoyment thereof died leaving behind one son the plaintiff No. 1 and two daughters Aziful Bibi, Karful Bibi, and a wife Meherjan as his heirs; Karful Bibi died unmarried leaving behind her mother Meherjan, brother the plaintiff No. 1 and a sister Aziful Bibi the plaintiff No. 2. Thereafter, Meherjan died leaving behind the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 as her sole heirs; it is also stated by the plaintiffs that during S.A. Operation plaintiffs share was wrongly recorded as 2 annas 13 gondas 1 Kara and 1 Karanti. Though as a matter of fact the remaining 2 annas 13 gondas 1 Kara 1 Karanti share was wrongly recorded in favour of some of the defendants as also in favour of the predecessors of some others, who have no right, title, interest or possession therein; it was further stated in the plaint that on 13.5.1985 when the defendants attempted to invade the right of the plaintiffs over the suit land on the basis of such erroneous record of right the plaintiffs brought the suit claiming their title in the suit land which has been in their possession, as stated above. 

3. The defendant No. 4 entered appearance upon filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the plaintiffs have no right, title interest or possession in the suit land appertaining to C.S. Khatian Nos. 17,217,218 and 219 rather one Alef Chowkider was the exclusive owner in possession of the said land; said Alef Chowkider married Mayjan the mother of one Sharap Ali who was the grandfather of defendant No. 4 while Araj Ali is the son of Mohammed Jan who was the former husband of Maynajan. It was further alleged in the written statement that one third share was collusively recorded in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs during C.S. operation which was not correct; Alef Chowkider gifted away some land to the extent of 1.52 acres in favour of Sahraf Ali by a deed of gift dated 14 Falgoon 1326 B.S. and had handed over possession; it was also stated in the written statement that Araj Ali also executed a nadabinama in respect of the said land in favour of Sworup Ali on 28 Chaitra, 1344 B.S. Subsequently the S.A. record was correctly prepared in his favour, the plaintiffs have no right, title, interest or possession in the suit land, hence the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

4. It was also stated in the written statement that a suit being Title Suit No. 106 of 1968 was instituted by the plaintiffs in respect of selfsame land against the defendants but it was withdrawn on 27.3.1969 with a permission of sue afresh as such the instant suit is also barred by limitation. 

5. Eventually, the suit was taken up for hearing by the Assistant Judge where the plaintiffs examined 3 witnesses while the defendants examined 4 witnesses on their behalf and upon conclusion of the trial the Assistant Judge decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 24.9.91 in Title Suit No. 81 of 1985. 

6. As against the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 24.9.1991 passed by the trial Court the defendant No. 4 as appellant preferred Title Appeal No. 144 of 1991 before the District Judge, Patuakhali which on transfer was heard by the Subordinate Judge, Patuakhali who having heard the appeal allowed the same by his Judgment and decree dated 14.7.1992, reversing the decree of the trial court. 

7. As against the aforesaid judgment and decree of reversal dated 14.7.1992 passed in Title Appeal No. 144 of 1991, the Plaintiffs as petitioners obtained the instant rule. 

8. Mr. Golam Arshed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the impugned judgment and decree as passed by the appellate court below is not a proper judgment of reversal in that it is violative of the mandatory provision of Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In elaborating his submission the learned Advocate submits further that the trial Court upon consideration of the evidence and materials on record arrived at a positive finding to the effect that the plaintiffs have been able to established their right, title and possession in the suit land but the appellate court reversed the decision of the trial court without adverting to the aforesaid finding arrived at by the trial court rather affirmed those findings in his judgment. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits further that the appellate court below allowed the appeal upon reversing the decision of the trial court merely on the point of limitation erroneously holding that the suit is barred by limitation. In substantiating his submission the learned Advocate referred to the finding of the appellate court below to the effect that the previous suit namely title Suit No. 106 of 1968 was withdrawn on 27.3.1969 with a permission to sue afresh on the same cause of action with a condition to pay Rupees 50 to the credit of the contesting defendant, but the instant suit being Title Suit No. 21 of 1985 had been instituted on 3.8.1985 long after an interval of about 16 (sixteen) years as such the suit was, according to the Appellate Court, barred by limitation. Mr. Golam Arshed, the learned Advocate submits that the instant suit being Title Suit No. 81 of 1985 is neither filed on the same cause of action nor the relief claimed in the earlier suit is the same as that of the present one. According to the learned Advocate the previous suit was filed on a different cause of action accrued at that relevant time while the present suit has been filed with the cause of action accrued on 13.5.1985 on which date the defendants threatened to invade the right of the plaintiffs over the suit land. The learned Advocate submits further that in the previous suit the relief claimed was that of correction of record of right and declaration of title while in the present suit the plaintiffs have simply prayed for declaration of their title in the suit land and no prayer for correction of record of right has been made. Therefore, the learned Advocate submits that the subject matter in the previous suit with that the present suit is not the same and in substantiating his submission the learned Advocate refers to the decision of Bhagavan Das Mohesri Vs. Prosannan Dev Raiket and others reported in AIR 1934 Calcutta 433. Wherein a Division Bench of Calcutta High Court relying on AIR 1917 Born 10 and 431. C 752 followed the decision to the effect. 

"The question is whether the previous suit was a suit for the same "subject matter" within the meaning of 0.23. R.I. We are of opinion that "subject-matter " means, to use the word of 1. I, R.I, the series of acts or transactions alleged to exits giving rise to the relief claimed. Obviously, the first series of acts or transactions which formed the basis of the first suit was in-complete, or the plaintiff would have been able to prosecute his suit to decree. It was incomplete because there was no notice to quit. The second series of acts of transactions is complete because the notice to quit has been given, and therefore, the two suits are not in respect of the same "subject-matter". 

9. In this case no one has appeared on behalf of the opposite parties to oppose the Rule despite due service of notice upon them. Under such circumstances I have myself gone through the materials on record including the impugned judgments passed by the Courts below as also heard by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. 

10. Upon consideration of the aforesaid materials and submission of the learned advocate for the petitioner particularly when lie relief upon the decision given by a Division Bench of Calcutta High Court as referred to above. Wherefrom I find that the said decision has got a direct bearing in the present case. More particularly when the earlier suit being Title Suit No. 106 of 1968 was a suit for correction of record of right disclosing a particular cause of action arose in the year 1968 while the present suit being Title Suit No. 81 of 1985 was instituted seeking a decree for simple declaration of title on the basis of a cause of action which arose on 13.5.1985 when a threat of invasion of the right of the plaintiffs was demonstrated by the defendants then only the plaintiffs took recourse to institution of the present suit. This Court being in respectful agreement with the principle of law enunciated in the case referred to above, also finds that the expression subject matter as used in order 23 rule 1 means a series of acts or transactions alleged to exist giving rise to the relief claimed. As such the first series of facts or transactions, which formed the basis of the first suit being Title suit No. 106 of 1968 was based on erroneous record of right, in the S.A. Khatian and the suit was brought from the date of Knowledge with respect to such wrong record of right but in the instant suit namely Title Suit No. 81 of 1985 the date of threatened invasion over the right of the plaintiffs on 13.5.1985 was the cause of action and not the erroneous record or right, besides the relief claimed in that suit cannot be said to be one and the same. Therefore in my opinion the previous suit was instituted with a different subject matter then that of the present suit and that the relief claimed in that suit is not the same as in the present case besides, the cause of action in that suit is not the same as in the present one. Therefore, institution of the previous suit cannot have any bearing in instituting the present suit and in that view of the matter the institution of the previous suit cannot be a ground for treating the present suit as one barred by limitation, under Article 122 of the Limitation Act. 

11. It has also been noticed that the appellate court did not find any reason to differ with the trial court in respect of title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land rather the finding of the trial court in that respect has been concurrently affirmed by the appellate court yet dismissed the suit merely on the ground of limitation which in my opinion has been arrived at one misconception of the provision of law as embodied in both Article 122 of the Limitation Act as also of the expression used in Order 23 Rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure. In view of the discussions made above the impugned judgment and decree of reversa call for any interference by this court. 

12. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and decree of reversal dated 14.7.1992 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, now Joint District Judge in Title Appeal No. 144 of 1991 is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree dated 24.9.1991 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Galachipa in Title Suit No. 81 of Title Suit No. 81 of 1985 is hereby upheld. 

Send down a copy of this judgment along with the Lower Courts Record to the trial court at once.

End.

parties:
Regent Ken International Ltd. ------ Defendant-Petitioner.
Vs.
Amanat Shah Ship Breaking Industries Ltd.----- Plaintiff Opposite Party.
full_judgment:
Md. Imman Ali, J: This Miscellaneous Case arises out an application under Order IX, Rule 13 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte judgment and decree dated 18.5.21004 and 29.8.2004 respectively passed by this Hon'ble Court in Admiralty Suit No. 5 of 2004.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Miscellaneous Case are that the opposite party as plaintiff, instituted Admiralty Suit No. 5 of 2004 against the vessel M.V. Accord for recovery of Tk. 1.83.62.477/- for the supply of necessaries as well as for their services rendered to the vessel Service of notices was effected upon the defendants including the defendant-petitioner, through his local agent, namely, viking Associates Ltd., by means of hanging on their premises since they refused to accept the notices. This Court having found that the service was good decreed the suit ex-parte as no one appeared to defend the same.

3. Mr. Md. Moksadul Islam, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the owner of the vessel, defendant No. 3 petitioner, submits that the petitioner did not receive the notice of the admiralty Suit in question. He came to know recently about the ex parte decree and took steps to file this petition for restoration at the earliest opportunity. He submits that, although there was an order issued by this Honble Court to serve summons/notice upon the defendant petitioner, none was served nor did the defendant petitioner receive any summons/notice of the suit. On the contrary he was prevented from appearing since the so-called agent of the ship-owner did not accept the notice. He added that the agency agreement between the ship owner and Viking Associates Ltd. was terminated as soon as the consignment had been dealt with Moreover, he points out the so-called agent filled Admiralty Suit No. 16 of 2000 against the owner of the vessel (the instant petitioner) claiming their dues he submits that in such circumstances the agency agreement with Viking Associates Ltd would certainly have ceased, at the latest when they filed a suit against the owner. He further submits that the record shows that Viking Associates Ltd. Refused to accept the summons on behalf of Regent Ken International Ltd. and that confirms the fact that at the time of institution of Admiralty suit No. 5 of 2004 they were not the local agent for the petitioner and accordingly no summons was served upon the petitioner or the local agent and therefore the ex parte judgment and decree obtained fraudulently in the said suit is liable to be set aside for ends of justice. He submits that the petitioner has been able to prove that there was sufficient cause shown for not appearing in the suit.

4. Mr. SA Siddique, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party plaintiff, submits that the record shows and this Hon'ble Court accepted that the service upon the defendants was in accordance with law and hence proceeded to deliver judgment ex parte. He further pointed out that the judgment in Admiralty Suit No. 16 of 2000 leaves no question of doubt regarding the fact that Viking Associates Ltd. were duly appointed agents of Regent Ken International Ltd. and accordingly the service upon them was rightly accepted as being in accordance with law. On a separate issue the learned Advocates submits that the first Power of Attorney allegedly executed ,by the ship-owner is not in accordance with law since it was not revalidated and duly stamped as required by the provisions of Section 18 of the Stamp Act, 1899, which provides.

"18(1). Every instrument chargeable with duty and executed only out of (Bangladesh), and not being a bill of exchange, or promissory note, may be stamped within three months after it has been first received in Bangladesh."

5. The second Power of Attorney is also defective inasmuch as it does not show that the executant was residing in Bangladesh when he executed the same. Moreover, he submits, even if the second Power of Attorney was duly executed, it does not authorize the filing of the instant petition for restoration, which had been already filed before that Power of Attorney was executed. In this regard the learned Advocate has referred to the unreported decision in Admiralty Suit No. 37 of 1999 (Judgment delivered on 9.8.2004). The learned advocate also submits that the petitioner is bound to show by cogent evidence as to when he came to know about the ex parte decree and to explain the delay in filing the Miscellaneous case for restoration. This not having been done, the present application is liable to be rejected.

6. With regard to the validity of the Power of Attorney, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the first Power of Attorney had been duly executed and although the learned Counsel for the opposite party had vehemently argued and raised objections against the filing of the same, the Hon'ble court rejected his contentions on the ground that there was nothing wrong in the Power of Attorney and the clerical errors, if there are any, can easily be corrected later by the defendant petitioner. With regard to the delay in filing this petition, the learned Advocate submits that he has explained that he filed the instant petition as soon as he was able to ascertain the fact that the suit had been decreed ex parte.

<u>7. I have considered the submissions of the learned advocates and pursued the petition as well as the written objection filed by the plaintiff opposite party and the reply of the petitioner to those written objection. It is undoubtedly true that Viking Associates Ltd. were appointed by Regent Ken international Ltd. as their local agent. That fact was established by the judgment and decree in Admiralty Suit No. 16 of 2000. However, it is equally clear that the interests of Viking Associates Ltd. became hostile to the owners of the ship, i.e. the petitioner, as and when they filed Admiralty Suit No. 16 of 2000 against the owners of the vessel. I am inclined to accept that the so-called agent's refusal to receive service of summons notices indicates their hostility towards the owners of the vessel. In such view of the matter, it follows that the owners were not properly served with notices of the suit. In the event that the petitioner was not served with the notices of this Court, the fact that the application for restoration was not filed within the statutory period of limitation is of little consequence. In this regard I may take support from the decision of the Appellate Division in the case of Abdul Rashid and another Vs. Abdul Batik and an-other, reported in 35 DLR(AD)162. In that case their Lordships held that due service of summons is an essential condition which must be satisfied before the Court proceeded to give a judgment under Order IX, Rule 13, if a party satisfies a court that summons were not duly served upon him, the Court is bound to set aside the ex parte decree. In such a case question of knowledge is not at all relevant and ex parte decree will be set aside even if the defendant had knowledge of institution of a suit. In the facts of the instant case, I am satisfied that the petitioner, who was defendant No. 3, was not served with notices of the suit nor the service upon Viking Associates Ltd. was effective service upon defendant No.3. It is patently clear that by the time Admiralty Suit No. 5 of 2004 was filed, the interests of Viking Associates Ltd. had already become hostile to the interests of Regent Ken International Ltd., as is apparent from the records of Admiralty Suit No. 16 of 2000. Hence I am satisfied that the defendant petitioner was not duly served notice of the suit and that was the cause for his non-appearance when the suit was called on for hearing.</u>

<u>8. With regard to the opposite party's challenge on the validity of the Power of Attorney, I am of the view that the decision referred by the learned advocate for the plaintiff is not applicable in the facts of the instant case, where the facts are quite different. It appears that in the instant case the Power of Attorney was typed on Bangladeshi stamp paper of Tk. 150/- and executed in Hong Kong where it was endorsed before the Bangladeshi Consulate and subsequently endorsed by the Foreign Ministry in Dhaka. According to the provisions of Section 18 of the Stamp Act, 1899 an instrument executed abroad is required to be stamped within 3 months by the Collector for it to be admissible in evidence. In the instant case it appears that the instrument had been typed on stamped paper issued by the government of Bangladesh and, therefore, revenue, in this case to the tune of Tk. 150/-. had already been paid to the appropriate authority. Moreover the provisions of Sections 33 and 35 allow for admission of instruments upon impounding on payment of the date stamp duty and fine for delay in payment. In the facts of the present case it appears that when the first Power of Attorney was produced before this Court the same was accepted and the constituted Attorney was permitted to swear the affidavit in connection with the application for restoration. It appears to me that thereby the Power of Attorney has been accepted and cannot again be questioned in the same proceedings as provided by section 36 of the Stamp Act. In such view of the matter, I am inclined to accept that the Power of Attorney filed by the petitioner has been accepted and since the instrument was executed on stamp paper issued by the Bangladesh government, if at all, it is simply a question of paying the balance Stamp duty under Section 18 of the Stamp Act as provided by section 33 of that Act. In any event such technical defects should not be allowed to defeat the application if there is found merit in it. I may also take support from the decision in the case of Manager, Jammu & Kashmir. State Property in Pakistan Vs. Khuda Yar and another reported in PLD 1975 SC 678 where it was observed that mere technicalities should not be allowed to stand in the way of justice. It is my view that the defect in the Power of Attorney for not correctly stamping the same can be cured by the production of the instrument before the appropriate authority and by paying the deficit stamp duty and fine, if any, payable in accordance with Section 33 and 35 of the Stamp Act, 1899.</u>

9. In view of the above discussion. I find merit in this application which is liable to be allowed.

10. In the result the miscellaneous case is allowed. The ex parte judgment and decree dated 18.5.2004 Admiralty Suit No. 5 of 2004 is hereby set aside. The said suit is restored to its original file and number. However, the petitioner is directed to the produce the instrument, namely the Power of Attorney executed abroad, before the Collector for the purpose of impounding the same and report compliance to this Court within 10 days, failing which this order of restoration shall stand vacated.

There will be no order as to costs.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Md. Omar Ali Khan, Advocate ----- For the petitioner
Mr. Md. Ibrahim Mollah, Advocate ----- For the opposite party
parties:
Ramija Khatun and another
Vs.
Abdul Aziz and others
full_judgment:
Md. Muzammel Hossain, J:- This rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order No. 11 dated 14.01.1997 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Gaffargaon, Mymensingh in Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 1996 rejecting the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure arising out of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. (35 of 1993)/(38 of 1993)  should not be set aside.

2. The present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as petitioners-instituted Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. (35 of 1993)/(38 of 1993)   against the other opposite parties. The opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 are the co-sharers of the suit land but the suit land was transferred to the stranger purchasers. The aforesaid pre-emption case was contested by opposite party No. 11 denying the case of the pre-emptors-petitioners opposite party Nos. 1 and 2. The further case of the said opposite party No. 11 is that there was defect of parties in the preemption case as the heirs of opposite party No. 7 Md. Abdul Barek had not been added as opposite parties after his death. During the pendency of the pre-emption case the opposite party No. 7 submitted an application before the trial Court stating, inter alia, that since before the alleged transfer of the case land to opposite party No. 11 he has been in possession of 4.25 acres of land in the disputed jote. His further case is that he is a bonafide cultivator and does not possess the land exceeding 50 standard bighas and he is a co-sharer by purchase. At the time of transfer no notice was served upon him as per provision of law. He submitted an application to allow him to join as cosharer under subsection (4) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In the mean time the aforesaid opposite party Md. Abdul Barek died and the present petitioners were added as parties in the said case but no notice was served upon them. The learned trial Court was pleased to allow the pre-emption case by judgment and order dated 24.4.1996. Thereafter the present petitioners as the heirs of said opposite party Abdul Barek submitted an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code being Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 1996 before the trial court for setting aside the aforesaid order of preemption. The learned Senior Assistant Judge Gaffargaon by the impugned judgment and order dated 14.1.1997 dismissed Miscellaneous Case No.21 of 1996.

3. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order dated 14.01.1997 the present petitioners preferred the revisional application before this Court and obtained the instant Rule

4. Mr. Md. Omar Ali Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the learned Senior Assistant Judge committed an error of law in rejecting the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code with the findings that the petitioners did not prove that the summons were not served upon them and thereby shifted burden of proof on the petitioners from the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 and thus committed an error of law which has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He then submits that the learned Senior Assistant Judge committed an error of law by misconstruing and misinterpreting the law and facts of the case and material evidence on record and came to an erroneous decision which has resulted in an error in decision occasioning failure of justice. He finally submits that the impugned judgment and order suffers from contradictory findings and the learned Senior Assistant Judge committed an error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order which has occasioned failure of justice and as such the Rule should be made absolute.

5. Mr. Md. Ibrahim Mona, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that the learned Senior Assistant Judge committed no error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order which does not require any interference by this Court and as such the rule is liable to be discharged.

6. I have perused the revisional application with the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge in Misc. Case No. 21 of 1996 arising out of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. (35 of 1993)/(38 of 1993)   I have also perused the Lower Court record.

7. In this particular case the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as petitioners instituted Pre-emption Miscellaneous  No. (35 of 1993)/(38 of 1993)   against the other opposite parties. The present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 are the co-sharers of the suit land but the suit land was transferred to strangers. They want pre-emption of the suit land. The case was contested by the opposite party No. 11 denying the case of the preemptors petitioners opposite party No. 1 and 2. It was contended on behalf of the opposite party No. 11 that the pre-emption case suffers from defect of party as the heirs of the opposite party No. 7 had not been added as parties after his death. It is stated that during the pendency of the pre-emption case the opposite party No. 7 had filed an application before the trial Court stating that since before the alleged transfer of the case land to opposite party No. 11, he had been in possession of 4.25 acres of land in the disputed jote. The opposite party No. 7 was a bonafide cultivator and did not possess the land exceeding 50 standard bighas and he was a co-sharer by purchase. At the time of transfer no notice was served upon him as per provision of law. He filed an application for allowing him to join as a co-sharer under Sub-section (4) of Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It is further stated that the petitioners' predecessor Abdul Barek died and the present petitioners were added as parties in the pre-emption case but no notice was served upon them. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Gaffargaon by judgment and order dated 24.4.1996 allowed the pre-emption case on contest against the opposite party No. 11 and exparte against the heirs of the opposite party No. 7- petitioners. Thereafter the present petitioners filed' an application under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 1996 for setting the aforesaid judgment and order dated 24.4.1996, which was passed exparte against them.

8. On perusal of the case record of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. (35 of 1993)/(38 of 1993)   it appears that the case was allowed against the opposite party Nos. 11 and 13 on contest and exparte against the opposite party Nos. 1-l0. Thereafter the present petitioners as the heirs of opposite party No. 7 Abdul Barek filed the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code for setting aside the aforesaid judgment and order dated 24.4.1996 passed in pre-emption case and the said application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 1996 on 24.6.1996. On perusal of the record of Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 1996 it appears that on 7.10.1996 the present petitioner No. 2 was examined as P.W. 1 and the case was heard exparte against the opposite parties. The learned Assistant Judge by order dated 7.10.1996 observed, inter alia, that

"প্রার্থীপক্ষের জবানবন্দী নথীভূক্ত রাথা হউক। প্রার্থীপক্ষ আদেশের জাবেদা নকল, সমন জারী প্রদিবেদনের জাবেদা নকল দাখিল করে নাই। যেহেতু মূল নথী আপীলে গিয়াছে সেইহেতু উক্ত কাগজপত্র ছাড়া সিদ্ধান্তে আসা যাইতেছে না। আগামী ১৭/১০/৯৬ইং তারিখ কাগজপত্র দাখিল ও আদেশ।"

9. On perusal of the order dated 17.10.96 it appears that the petitioners prayed for time to file the required documents and the trial court allowed the prayer fixing the case on 29.10.1996for filing documents and order. On 29.10.1996 the petitioners again prayed for time and the Court adjourned the case to 16.11.1996 for submission of documents and order. On 16.11.1996 the petitioners failed to file the required documents and prayed for time and the Court allowed the prayer fixing the case on 28.11.1996. On 28.11.1996 the petitioners also failed to submit the documents and prayed for time and the Court again allowed time fixing the case on 14.1.1996 for submission of documents and order. On perusal of the impugned order dated 14.1.1996 it appears that on that date the petitioners submitted photostat copies of the judgment and order dated 24.4.1996 passed in Preemption Miscellaneous Case No. (35 of 1993)/(38 of 1993)   and no other document was filed on behalf of the petitioners. The learned Senior Assistant Judge having considered the deposition of p. w. 1 taken on 7.10.1996, application for restoration (plaint of Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 1996) and other materials on record observed that the petitioners failed to comply 'With the order dated 7.10.1996 in submitting the certified copy of the report of process server and also certified copy of the judgment and order passed in Preemption Case No. (35 of 1993)/(38 of 1993). Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code provides that-

"In any case in which a decree is passed exparte against a defendant, he may apply to the Court by which the decree was passed for an order to set it aside; and if he satisfies the Court that the summons was not duly served, or that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing, the Court shall make an order setting aside the decree as against him upon such terms as to costs, payment into Court or otherwise as it thinks fit, and shall appoint a day for proceeding with the suit;"

10. In the instant case the present petitioners' case is that summons of the preemption case were not served upon them as a result of which they could not appear before the Court at the time of hearing of the case and the pre-emption case was allowed exparte against the petitioners. On perusal of the deposition of the present petitioner No. 2 as p.w.1 in the Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 1996 it appears that he stated that summons were not served upon them and they were seriously prejudiced by the exparte order. I have already noticed that the petitioners failed to comply with the court's order in submitting certified copies of the report of the process server, judgment and order dated 24.4.1996 passed in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. (35 of 1993)/(38 of 1993)  and the order sheets of the 38 of 1993 aforesaid pre-emption case. The learned Senior Assistant Judge observed that the petitioner failed to prove that summons were not served upon them and the petitioners also failed to prove that they for the first time on 20.6.1996 came to know about the judgment and order dated 24.6.1996 passed in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. (35 of 1993)/(38 of 1993).

<u>11. Under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code the petitioners were required to prove that summons were not duly served upon them or that they were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the case was called on for hearing. In a number of cases including the case of Abdur Rashid and another Vs. Abdul Barik and another reported in 4 BLD (AD) 83 it has been held that if a party satisfies a Court that summons were not duly served upon him, the Court is bound to set aside exparte decree. In the case of Juran Chandra Mondal Vs. Rabindra Nath Mondal reported in 5 BLD (1985) 126 it has been held that when a party satisfies the Court that summons was duly served upon him the Court is bound to set aside the exparte decree. In the instant case before us it appears that the Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 1996 was heard exparte against the opposite parties by examining the present petitioner No. 2 as P.W.I on 7.10.1996. Thereafter, to facilitate the petitioners the Court allowed them 5 adjournments to file certified copies of the report of the process server, judgment and order dated 24.4.1996 and order sheets of the Miscellaneous Case No. (35 of 1993)/(38 of 1993)  to ascertain as to whether the summons were duly served upon them or not. But in-spite of allowing several adjournments the petitioners failed to submit the aforesaid certified copies and thereby the present petitioners failed to prove that summons were not duly served upon them. In view of the above findings and observation I am of the view that the learned Senior assistant Judge has rightly found that the petitioners failed to prove that the summons were not served upon them and the petitioners failed to prove that they for the first time on 20.6.1996 came to know about the judgment and order dated 24.4.1996 passed in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. (35 of 1993)/(38 of 1993)  and accordingly the present Miscellaneous case was rightly dismissed by the impugned judgment and order dated 14.1.1996. 1 do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment and order dated 14.1.1996 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Gafargaon.</u>

12. In the result, the rule is discharged without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and order dated 14.1.1996 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Gaffargaon in Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 1996 is hereby affirmed.

Send down the lower Court records with a copy of this judgment expeditiously.

End.

full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha, J: This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 14.6.1995 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Noakhali in Title Appeal No. 285 of 1992 reversing the judgment and decree dated 12.5.1992 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Noakhali in Title Suit No. 403 of 1987 sending back the case on remand to trial court.

2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit in the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Noakhali being Title Suit No. 403 of 1987, against opposite parties No. 3-9 for declaration of title in the suit land measuring 1.08 acres described in the schedule of the plaint stating inter alia that Ram Kanai Shil, grand father of the petitioner was the original owner of the suit land by way of settlement from the Zaminder on executing kabuliayt in 1322 B.S. and since then he has been owning and possessing the same on payment of rent to the landlords and living there with the member of his family after constructing dwelling huts therein. It has been alleged that the M.R.R. khatian has been wrongly prepared in the names of the defendants and hence the suit for declaration of title for removing the cloud cast over their title.

3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statements denying all the material allegations of the plaint and contended inter alia that the suit as framed is not maintainable in law and it is barred by limitation. It has been contended that the suit land has been rightly recorded in the M.R.R. Khatian in the names of the defendants who own and possess the same in their own right. The plaintiff has no right, title and possession in the suit and the plaintiff filed the suit against the defendants on false and frivolous allegations for illegal gains.

4. The learned Senior Assistant Judge decreed the suit exparte on 12.5.1992 on the evidence of P.W.1 and on consideration of the papers and documents proved by the plaintiff. Against the aforesaid decree defendant No. 1 filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the exparte decree whereupon Misc. Case No. 65 of 1992 was started. It was alleged that although he had attained majority before the filing of the suit, no summons was served upon him and as such the impugned order is liable to be set aside. It was also alleged that due to serious illness being attacked with jaundice, he could not appear before the Court when the exparte decree on 12.5.1992 was passed.

5. The plaintiff-petitioner contested the Miscellaneous case by filing written objection denying all its material allegations contending inter alia that the summons was duly served upon the defendant and there is no illegality in the impugned judgment and decree. Miscellaneous Case No. 65 of 1992 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Civil Procedure was ultimately dismissed on 2.11.1992 but defendant No. 1 did not take any further step against the aforesaid order of dismissal before any superior Court as a result of which the ex-part decree passed on 12.5.92 got confirmed. Thereafter the 2 strangers named Nurul Hoque and Mohammad Rafiqullah, who were never parties in the suit filed Title Appeal No. 285 of 1992 before the District Judge, Noakhali against the aforesaid exparte decree dated 12.5.1992 made in Title Suit No. 402 of 1997 contending inter alias that respondent No. 2 Biplab Kumar Shil during his minority inherited the suit property along with others. On attaining majority he transferred 3’15 1⁄2 acres of land, including a portion of the homestead, to them by a registered Kabala dated 26.5.1992 and

since they have been owning and possessing the same. It has been alleged that for the first time on 26.10.1992 they learnt from the people of the locality that respondent No. 1 had obtained a collusive exparte decree in respect of the suit property and hence the appeal.

6. The learned Subordinate Judge by the impugned judgment dated 14.6.1995 allowed the appeal and sent the case back on remand.

7. Mr. Nikhilesh Dutta, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the learned Subordinate Judge passed the impugned order of remand illegally and arbitrarily without at all considering the evidence on record as required by Order 41 Rule 31 C.P.C. and the same has occasioned failure of justice.

No one appears to oppose the Rule.

8. Mr. Nikhilesh Dutta, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, placed before me the impugned judgment. It appears that the learned Subordinate Judge passed the impugned order of remand essentially on the ground of avoiding multiplicity of litigations between the parties. In view of fact that opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 were not parties in the original Title Suit No. 403 of 1987, nor they were parties in Miscellaneous case No. 65 of 1992 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure there cannot be any justification for sending back the case on remand to the trial Court to give unwanted opportunity to opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 in the name of avoiding multiplicity of suits. The learned Subordinate Judge did not find any illegality or legal infirmity in the impugned judgment passed by the learned trial Court providing justifiable ground for setting it aside.

<u>9. It is a settled proposition of law that any judgment or order passed by any Court, whether contested or exparte, has a sanctity in the eye of law and an exparte decree or order is as good as a contested one until it is set aside by any competent Court on legal grounds.</u>

<u>10. The law of remand is regulated by Order 41 Rule 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure and under exceptional circumstances the provision of section 151 of the Code is re-sorted to for preventing an injustice or an abuse of the process of the Court. The impugned order of remand is not covered by either of the above provisions of law and as such it cannot be sustained, it being patently illegal and arbitrary. The impugned order has in deed occasioned failure of justice.</u>

11. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and decree dated 14.6.95 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Noakhali in Title Appeal no. 285 of 1992 sending the case back on remand to the trial Court on reversing the judgment and decree dated 12.5.92 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Noakhali in Title Suit No. 403 of 1987 are set aside and the decree passed in Title Suit No. 403 of 1987 is hereby maintained.

Send down the lower Court records at once.

End.
