Anwara Begum and ors.
Vs.
Shahnewaj and ors.
full_judgment:
Sheikh Rezowan Ali, J: On an application by the petitioners under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure a rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 18.7.2002 passed in Miscellaneous appeal No. 241 of 2001 by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court affirming those dated 17.10.2001 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 39 of 1985 (a proceedings under order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure) by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd  Court, Dhaka dismissing the said Miscellaneous case should not be set aside and /or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court might seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this revisional application, in short, are that the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted title suit No. 363 of 1981 (later re-numbered as Title Suit No. 491 of 1981 in the 4th Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Dhaka) against the present petitioners as defendants for a decree of Specific Performance of Contract in respect of certain land. The said suit was decreed exparte on 1.10.1984. On 29.11.1984 petitioner No.1 Anowara Begum preferred a petition under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure giving rise of Miscellaneous Case No. 96 of 1984 for setting aside of the said exparte decree and for restoration of the suit to its original file and number for rehearing on the ground of her inability to appear before the Court for illness when the suit was called on for hearing.

3. The opposite party No. 1 filed a written objection in the said proceeding under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure denying the alleged fact of illness of the petitioner No. 1. According to him the suit was rightly decreed exparte on account of the petitioner No. 1 having not been prevented by any sufficient Case from appearing before the Court when the suit was called on for hearing.

4. During the course of trial the petitioner No. 1 examined 2 witnesses including herself. The opposite party No. 1 however, did not examine any witness but his learned Advocate cross-examined the P.Ws. at length. On the assessment of the evidence on record the learned Joint. District Judge found that the petition under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was barred by limitation and that the petitioner No. 1 could not prove the fact of her illness preventing her from appearing before the Court hence the suit was called on for hearing.

5. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order of the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd  Court, Dhaka the instant petitioners preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 241 of 2002 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka, who ultimately transferred the appeal to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka, Learned Additional District Judge by his impugned judgment and order passed on 18.7.2002 dismissing the appeal mainly on the ground that the petitioner No. 1 could not prove the fact of her illness and that though a medical certificate was submitted it was not proved by the physician who issued such certificate. Consequently she failed to prove that she was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing before the Court below when the suit was called on for hearing.

6. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned lower Appellate Court the petitioners preferred the instant revisional application and obtained the present Rule.

7. It has been submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that learned lower Appellate Court illegal/refused to consider the medical certificate which was produced before the trial Court by the petitioner No. 1 in support of her illness preventing her from appearing before the Court at the material time. In this connection he has cited a decision in the case of Khleda Roushan Asa Vs. Md. Nurul Haq, reported in (1990) 10 BLD(AD) at page 242 and another decision in the case of M/S, Jaidurga Industries, Joypore and another -Vs. Union Bank of India reported in AIR 1988(Orissa) at Page 104.

8. Learned Advocate for the opposite party, on the other hand, has submitted that the Medical Certificate submitted in the Court below was not admissible in evidence without examination of the physician who issued such certificate. In support of his submission he has cited a decision in the case of Kutubuddin Ahmed Siddiky -Vs. East Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation, reported in 27 DLR(1975) at Page. 433.

<u>9. We have given our active consideration to the submissions made by the learned Advocates for both the sides and the case laws cited by them as described above. The rulling reported in 10 BLD (AD) 242 relates to a case where adjournment was not allowed to the party willing to examine the physician who issued medical certificate, in support of his illness. It does not appear to us that the said decision exempted examination of the medical Officer towards admission of a medical certificate in evidence when it was submitted by the party himself. The said decision does not fit in with the facts and circumstances of our instant case. The ruling reported in AIR 1988(Orissa) 104 does not relate to examination or non-examination of any physician towards admissibility or inadmissibility of any medical certificate in evidence. It is not relevant for our present purpose. On the other hand, in the decision re, oiled in 27 DLR at Page-433 it has been held by a Division Bench of this Court to the effect "Medical Certificate about the illness of a certain person and his inability to move is not admissible in evidence without the examination of the Medical Officer giving the certificate in Court". This being the legal position up to date regarding necessity of examination of a Medical Officer in support of the Medical Certificate issued by him we are constrained to hold both the Courts below were quite justified in refusing to accept and consider as evidence the Medical Certificate submitted by the party herself (petitioner No. 1) without examination of the Medical Officer who issued such certificate. Since the Medical Certificate was not proved according to law both the Courts below rightly discarded the same as any evidence of illness of the petitioner. Therefore, they rightly held that the petitioners failed to prove that she (petitioner No. 1) was prevented by, any sufficient cause from appearing before the court when the suit was called on for hearing. It does not appear to us that any error of law has been committed resulting in an error in decision occasioning miscarriage of justice. We find no merit in this revisional application.</u>

10. Accordingly, the rule is discharged with cost. The impugned judgment and order of the learned lower Appellate Court passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 241 of 2001 is upheld hereby. Earlier order passed by this Court staying all further proceedings of Execution Case No. 81 of 1985 pending in the 2nd Court of learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka is hereby vacated.

Communicate the order to the Courts below at once.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Azmalul Hossain, with Mr. ABM Siddiqur Rahman, Advocates ------ For the petitioner in W.P. No. 3016 of 2004

With

full_judgment:
Mirza Hossain Haider, J: This two writ petitions having arisen out of the same facts and relating to the same property which was put into auction and the respondent No. 5 and 6 of the Writ Petition No. 3016 of 2004 being the petitioners in Writ Petition No. 5961 of 2004, and the Petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3016 of 2004 being one of the respondents in Writ Petition No. 5961 of 2004, and the Petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3016 of 2004 being one of the respondents in Writ Petition No. 5961 of 2004 both these Rules are taken up together and disposed of by this single judgment upon stating the facts and circumstances chronologically.

2. In Writ Petition No. 3016 of 2004, Rule has been obtained by Arab Bangladesh Bank, a financial institution incorporated under the laws of the land, calling upon the respondent No. 1 i.e. the Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 3. Dhaka "to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 69 dated 28.10.2003 (Annexure-G) passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka, respondent No. 1 in Money Execution Case No. 126 of 2000 rejecting the application filed by the petitioner under Section 33(7) of the Act as well as for setting aside the order No. 63 dated 28.09.2003 (Annexure-F) passed by the said Court should note declared to have been made without lawful authority an of no legal effect ..."

3. Facts required for the disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the petitioner bank instituted Title Suit No. 32 of 1996 in the Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka against respondent Nos. 2, 3, 4 and others as defendants for realisation of outstanding dues amounting to Tk. 16,69,449.23 as on 31.12.95 and other necessary reliefs. The suit was ultimately heard and decreed ex parte on 14.11.1999 in favour of the plaintiff bank. The preliminary decree was drawn up on 18.11.1999 pursuant to the same and the final decree was drawn and signed on 15.10.2000. The respondent No. 2 i.e. the judgment debtor having failed to adjust the outstanding dues/decretal dues within the stipulated time as fixed by the Adalat in the decree, the petitioner bank put the said decree into execution vide Money execution Case No. 126 of 2000 for realization of the decretal dues amounting to Tk. 29,05,334, 25 as on 30.11.2000.

4. In the execution case several dates were fixed for sale of the mortgaged property by auction upon publishing the auction notice in accordance with law but sufficient bidders having not responded the same could not be sold at a reasonable price earlier. Then sale proclamation notice was published in newspapers fixing 28.9.2003 as the fresh date for auction when several bidders participated and respondent Nos. 5 and 6 jointly quoted Tk. 20,00,000.00 which was found to be the highest bid and was accepted by the Adalat. On 26.10.2003 the petitioner bank filed an application under section 33(2) and section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for cancellation of the bid dated 28.09.2003 and for taking necessary steps for re-auction of the said property in accordance with law. The said application was kept for hearing on 28.10.2003 when the decree holder bank, (the petitioner herein filed another application under section 33(7) of the Ain 2003 investing the property upon the decree holder bank by selling aside the auction. Both the applications of the petitioner bank were heard and rejected by the executing court on 28.10.2003 and accordingly the sale was also confirmed. Subsequently, the sale became absolute under Order XXI Rule 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Accordingly, sale certificate (Bomanama) was issued in favour of the respondent Nos. 5 and 6. The sale certificate was then sent for registration to the Sutrapur Sub-Registration Office on 15.11.2003.

5. The petitioner being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of rejection of the application filed under section 33(2) and (7) of the Ain and also the order of confirmation of sale by the executing court dated 28.10.2003, moved this Court under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule on 12.06.2004 and also obtained an order of stay of the operation of order No. 63 dated 28.9.2003 so far it relates to the acceptance of the bid in execution case till disposal of the Rule.

6. It is further stated in the aforesaid writ Petition that one Afroza Zaman, a third party along with another, in the meantime filed Writ Petition No. 6536 of 2003 before the High Court Division challenging the aforesaid sale of the mortgaged property to the present respondents No. 5 and 6 on the ground that the Adalat was wrong in accepting the bid of the present respondents Nos. 5 and 6 since the said writ petitioner Afroza Zaman and another had proprietary interest in the mortgaged property. The said Rule was contested by the present respondents Nos. 5 and 6 wherein, it was categorically stated that the bid was duly accepted and confirmed; the bid money was fully paid up by the purchasers whereupon the sale certificate has already been issued and registered. However, upon considering the entire facts and circumstances placed before the court and upon hearing the parties, including the decree holder bank (the present petitioner) the rule in Writ Petition No. 6536 of 2003 was discharged by judgment and order dated 15.6.2004.

7. On the other hand the petitioner bank filed another suit being Title Suit No. 97 of 1998 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka against one Sandra Enterprises Limited and its Directors and guarantors for realization of Tk. 60,58,198.08 as on 31.03.1996. The said suit was also decreed ex parse on 22.04.1999 and the decree was put into execution vide Execution Case No. 1257 of 2005. 17. Upon hearing the learned advocates for the parties and on perusal of the writ petitions, affidavit in oppositions, supplementary affidavit along with all the annexures appended therein, it appears that question has been raised as to firstly, whether the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 provides for holding of auction sale for more than once under section 33(1), (2) and (3) and under section 33(4), secondly, when section 33(7) can be invoked and thirdly, to construe section 33 whether "auction" is to be held or "auction sale" requires to be completed? To answer the aforesaid questions let us examine the provision of section 33 as a whole:

“৩৩। নিলাম বিক্রয়।– (১) অর্থ ঋণ আদালত ডিক্রি বা আদেশ জারীর সময় কোন সম্পত্তি বিক্রয়ের ক্ষেত্রে বাদীর খরচে বিজ্ঞপ্তি প্রচারের তারিখ হইতে অন্যূন ১৫ (পনের) দিবসের সময় দিয়া সীলমোহরকৃত টেন্ডার আহ্বান করিবে, উক্ত বিজ্ঞপ্তি কমপক্ষে বহুল প্রচারিত একটি বাংলা জাতীয় দৈনিক পত্রিকায়, তদুপরি ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে প্রয়োজন মনে করিলে স্থানীয় একটি পত্রিকায়, যদি থাকে, প্রকাশ করিবে; এবং আদালতের নোটিশ বোর্ডে লটকাইয়া ও স্থানীয়ভাবে ঢোল সহরতযোগেও উক্ত বিজ্ঞপ্তি প্রচার করিবে।

(২) প্রত্যেক দরদাতা উদ্ধৃত দরের ২৫% এর সমপরিমান টাকা জমানতস্বরূপ ব্যাংক ড্রাফট বা পে-অর্ডার আকারে আদালতের অনুকূলে দরপত্রের সহিত দাখিল করিবেন, দরপত্র সরাসরি দরপত্র বাক্সে কিংবা রেজিষ্ট্রিকৃত ডাকযোগে নির্ধারিত সময়ের মধ্যে নির্ধারিত কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট প্রেরণের মাধ্যমে দাখিল করিবেন, এবং দর গৃহীত হইবার পরবর্তী ১০ (দশ) দিবসের মধ্যে সমূদয় মূল্য পরিশোধ করিবেন এবং তাহা করিতে ব্যর্থ হইলে, আদালত তাঁহার উক্ত জামানতের টাকা বাজেয়াপ্ত করিবেঃ

তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, এই উপ-ধারার অধীন দরপত্রে সম্পত্তির প্রস্তাবকৃত মূল্য অস্বাভাবিকভাবে অপর্যাপ্ত বা কম প্রতীয়মান হইলে, আদালত, দরপ্রস্তাব বাতিল করিতে পারিবেন।

(৩) উপ-ধারা (২) এর অধীনে জামানত বাজেয়াপ্ত হইলে উহার অর্থ ডিক্রীদারকে প্রদান করা যাইবে, ডিক্রীকৃত দাবীর সহিত উক্ত সমন্বয় করা হইবে, এবং অতঃপর আদালত, দ্বিতীয় সর্বোচ্চ দরদাতা কর্তৃক উদ্ধৃত দর এবং পূর্বে বাজেয়াপ্তকৃত আমানত একত্রে সর্বোচ্চ দরদাতা কর্তৃক উদ্ধৃত দর অপেক্ষা কম না হইলে, উক্ত দ্বিতীয় সর্বোচ্চ দরদাতাকে সম্পত্তি নিলাম খরিদ করিতে আহ্বান করিবে এবং দ্বিতীয় সর্বোচ্চ দরদাতা আহুত হইবার পরবর্তী ১০ (দশ) দিবসের মধ্যে সম্পূর্ণ মূল্য পরিশোধ করিবেন এবং তাহা করিতে ব্যর্থ হইলে তাঁহার জামানত বাজেয়াপ্ত হইবে এবং জামানতের উক্ত অর্থ ডিক্রীদারকে ডিক্রীর দাবীর সহিত সমন্বয় করিবার জন্য প্রদান করা হইবে।

(৪) কোন সম্পত্তি উপ-ধারা (১), (২) ও (৩) এর বিধান অনুসারে নীলামে বিক্রয় করা সম্ভব না হইলে, আদালত পুনরায় কমপক্ষে বহুল প্রচারিত ২(দুই) টি বাংলা জাতীয় দৈনিক পত্রিকায়, তদুপরি ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে প্রয়োজন মনে করিলে স্থানীয় একটি পত্রিকায়, যদি থাকে, উপ-ধারা (১) এর অনুরূপ পদ্ধতিতে বিজ্ঞপ্তি প্রকাশ করাইয়া এবং আদালতের নোটিশ বোর্ডে নোটিশ টাংগাইয়া ও স্থানীয় ভাবে ঢোল সহরতযোগে সীলমোহরকৃত টেন্ডার আহবান করিবে, এবং বিক্রয় ও বাজেয়াপ্ত বিষয়ে উপ-ধারা (২) ও (৩) এ উল্লিখিত বিধান অনুসরণ করিবে।

(৫) কোন সম্পত্তি উপ-ধারা (১), (২), (৩) ও (৪) এর বিধান অনুসারে বিক্রয় করা সম্ভব না হইলে উক্ত সম্পত্তি, ডিক্রিকৃত দাবী পরিপূর্ণভাবে পরিশোধিত না হওয়া পর্যন্ত দখল ও ভোগের অধিকারসহ ডিক্রীদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত করা হইবে, এবং ডিক্রীদার উপ-ধারা (১), (২), (৩) ও (৪) এর বিধান অনুসারে উক্ত সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় করিয়া অপরিশোধিত ডিক্রীর দাবী আদায় করিতে পারিবে, এবং আদালত ঐ মর্মে একটি সার্টিফিকেট ইস্যু করিবে।

(৬) ডিক্রীকৃত অংকের অতিরিক্ত অর্থ বিক্রয় বাবদ আদায় হইলে উক্ত অতিরিক্ত অর্থ দায়িককে ফেরত প্রদান করিতে হইবে এবং ডিক্রীর দাবী অপেক্ষা কম হইলে অবশিষ্ট অর্থ বাবদ ২৮ ধারা বিধান সাপেক্ষে, আরো জারীর মামলা প্রহণযোগ্য হইবে।

(৭) উপ-ধারা (৪) ও (৫) এর বিধান সত্ত্বেও ডিক্রীদার, উল্লিখিত সম্পত্তি মালিকানা স্বত্ত্বে পাইতে আগ্রহী মর্মে আদালতের নিকট লিখিতভাবে আবেদন করিলে, আদালত, উপ-ধারা (১), (২), (৩) এর বিধানাবলীর কোনরূপ হানি না ঘটাইয়া, উপ-ধরা (৪) ও (৫) এর কার্যক্রম অনুসরন করা হইতে বিরত থাকিবে এবং ডিক্রীদারের প্রার্থিতমতে উল্লিখিত সম্পত্তির স্বত্ত্ব ডিক্রীদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত হইয়াছে মর্মে ঘোষণা প্রদানপূর্বক ততমর্মে একটি সনদপত্র জারী করিবে এবং জারীকৃত এইরূপ সনদপত্র স্বত্ত্বেও দলিল হিসাবে গণ্য হইবে এবং আদালত উহার একটি অনুলিপি সংশ্লিষ্ট স্থানীয় সাব-রেজিষ্টারের অফিসে নিবন্ধনের জন্য প্রেরন করিবে।

(৮) বর্তমান প্রচলিত অন্য কোন  আইনে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, উপ-ধারা (৭) এর অধীনে জারীকৃত সনদপত্র বাবদ কোন কর বা রেজিষ্ট্রেশন ফি আদায়যোগ্য হইবে না।

(৯) উপ-ধারা (৫) এর অধীন সম্পত্তির দখল ও ভোগের অধিকার অথবা উপ-ধারা (৭) এর অধীনে সম্পত্তির স্বত্ত্ব ডিক্রীদারের অনুকুলে ন্যস্ত হইলে, ধারা ২৮ এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, উক্ত ডিক্রী জারী মামলার চুড়ান্ত নিস্পত্তি হইবে।”

18. On perusal of the entire provision of section 33 as stated above it appears that the heading of the section is “���িলাম বিক্রয়” meaning "Auction sale". Thus it is clear that "auction" is not the subject matter in construing this provision but "auction sale" is to be construed. Moreover, section 33(1) provides the procedure of publishing notice for "sale". Similarly section 33(4) provides “নিলামে বিক্রয় সম্ভব না হইলে” meaning not possible to sell in auction an 33(5) provides for “বিক্রয় করা সম্ভব না হইলে।” meaning not possible to sell. So it appears that all these sub-sections deal with "sale of the property." Thus the contentions of Mr. Hossain that after the publication of the notice under section 33 (10) whether bidders appears or not auction is complete and if sale is not complete provision of section 33(4) will be invoked is not tenable in law. Hence, the contention of Mr. Bhuiyan that auction sale is to be completed appears to be more appropriate.

19. Reading the entire provision of section 33 it appears that procedure of auction sale has been categorically spelt out in the said section particularly in sub-sections (1), (2), (3) and (4) Pursuant to the sale proclamation published in one National Daily as contemplated in sub-section (1) sub section (2) comes into operation. Similarly, sub-section (3) comes into operation when the highest bidder fails to pay off the rest of the bid money within 10 days then the second highest bidder would be invited to purchase the same. Reading these two provisions we find that there must be at least two bidders. Again reading the proviso of sub section (2) we find that the Adalat has been given the discretion to cancel the sale bid in case the price is shockingly low meaning that the Court can exercise its discretion to cancel the bid, no matter whether the bid is contested by two bidders or more but only on consideration that the bid is too low. Thereafter sub-section (4) will come into operation in case the auction sale cannot be held under section 33 (1), (2) or (3) i.e. including cancellation of the bid on the ground that the price is too law. Reading all the aforesaid provisions it appears that the statute has given scope to the Adalat to hold auction more than once under section 33(1) (2) and (3) or under 33(4). The said view is fortified if we examine section 34(9) of the Ain which reads as follows:

“৩৪(৯) এই ধারা অধীনে কোন দায়িককে দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করার আদেশ প্রদান করিবে না, যদি না ততপূর্বে অন্ততঃ একটি নিলাম বিক্রয় কার্যক্রম অনুষ্ঠিত হইয়া থাকে এবং উহার দ্বারা ডিক্রীদারের প্রাপ্য পরিপূর্ণভাবে আদায় হইয়া থাকে।” meaning that at least one auction sale process is completed.

<u>20. So it appears that the aforesaid sub-section categorically says that minimum one sale process is to be taken place or completed. From the language used therein it is also clear that the Adalat has the power to hold auction sale more than once. Reading all the aforesaid provisions together we find that there is no scope to hold that more than one auction sale under the aforesaid provisions is barred.</u>

<u>21. On the other points, as agitated by the parties, we find that the sale has been held and accepted on 28.9.2003 and has been made absolute under Order XXI Rule 92 of the Code, on 28.10.2003 and prior to that, before 26.10.2003 no step was ever taken by the bank, as to the sale or as to the bid offered by the purchaser which has been accepted by the Adalat on the date of sale. Again on 28.10.2003, when the application dated 26.10.2003 was fixed for hearing the respondent bank came up with a fresh application under 33(7) without praying for setting aside the sale. The Adalat on the event of acceptance of the bid and having not raised any objection thereto by the bank on the dated of acceptance rejected the prayer under 33(7) and subsequent thereto, the boinama (the sale certificate) was issued and the same has been sent for registration. In consequence, with the confirmation of sale the same has become absolute and the mortgaged property sold in such auction in execution of the decree has already been vested on the purchaser from the date when the property was sold in auction i.e. on 28.9.2003 as contemplated in section 65 of the Code of Civil Procedure. So when the sale became absolute without any objection of the respondent Bank and the properly being vested with the purchaser no step under section 33(7) can be taken by the bank. The provision of invoking section 33(7) has been categorically spelt out in the said provision itself. It says-</u>

<u>“…আদালত, উপ-ধারা (১), (২), (৩) এর বিধানাবলীর কোনরূপ হানি না ঘটাইয়া উপ-ধারা (৪) ও (৫) এর কার্যক্রম অনুসরণ করা হইতে বিরত থাকিবে এবং ডিক্রীদারের প্রার্থিত মতে উল্লেখিত সম্পত্তির স্বত্ব ডিক্রীদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত হইয়াছে মর্মে ঘোষণা প্রদান পূর্বক ততমর্মে একটি সনদপত্র জারী করিবে এবং……..”</u>

<u>So it appears that the statute provides that the auction sale process is to be completed first under section 33(1),(2),(3) and in case of failure to sell the property under the said provisions right under section 33(7) can be exercised by the decree holder not prior to that. Again if the auction sale is complete then section 33(7) cannot be invoked. The right given under section 33(7) is a right given in favour of the decree holder so that when the property cannot be sold in auction and the decretal dues cannot be realized, the interest of the decree holder is not frustrated. Rather the decree holder can enjoy the benefit of the decree by enjoying the ownership of the property in any manner as its lawful owner.</u>

22. Therefore, the prayer for issuance of the certificate dated 28.10.2003 has been rightly rejected by the Adalat.

23. So far the question raised in Writ Petition No. 5961 of 2004, it appears that the properly in question is the same property which has already been sold in auction in Execution Case No. 126 of 2000 to the petitioners of the instant writ petition and the sale having already been made absolute the property sold in auction having already been vested in the petitioners the same cannot be put into auction sale in a subsequent execution case for execution of another decree, no matter whether the same is mortgaged to the bank in the subsequent suit. It was the duty of the bank to be more careful at the time of bringing the property in the first execution case, so that the decretal dues, if any, to the judgment debtor in any other suit, can also be realized by selling the same property which, according to the bank, was mortgaged by the judgment debtors in connection with three different transactions with the same bank. Thus the mortgaged property which is the subject matter of execution Case No. 126 of 2000 arising out of Title Suit No. 32 of 1996 auction sale of which has been challenged in Writ Petition No. 3016 of 2004 being the earlier transaction and the property being mortgaged if any, therein the subsequent mortgage of the same in connection with other transaction may be a second or third charge but the property initially mortgaged in connection with first one should be satisfied first then comes the question of second and third charge. In the instant cases it has not been spelt out by the bank whether the property is first, second or third charge. Even then with the execution of the decree in the earlier suit, where the property has been mortgaged and whose value is much higher than the accepted bid as alleged by the bank, we are afraid that the bank can get advantage since the property has already been sold and vested on the purchaser without any objection raised at the time of acceptance of bid. So, in this respect the impugned order dated 14.10.2004 challenged in Writ Petition 3961 of 2004 appears to have been passed completely without jurisdiction, because the property in execution Case No. 1257 of 2003 is the same property which has already been sold in auction much earlier to the auction purchaser i.e. the petitioners of Writ Petition No. 5961 of 2004 in Execution Case No. 126 of 2000 arising out of Title Suit No. 32 of 1996 between the same parties. As such the Adalat had no jurisdiction to issue certificate under section 33(7) in a property as the rule of the said property has already been vested upon the auction purchasers as provided in section 65 of the Code of Civil Procedure in accordance with law. Thus, the impugned order is illegal and without lawful authority.

24. For the reasons and discussions made hereinabove, we are of the view that the Rule in Writ Petition No. 3016 of 2004 has no merit and as such the same is liable to be discharged. The Rule in Writ Petition No. 5961 of 2004 bears merit and accordingly the same is liable to be made absolute.

25. In the result, the Rule in Writ Petition No. 3016 of 2004 is discharged and the Rule in Writ Petition No. 5961 of 2004 is made absolute.

26. There will be no order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the order No. 2 dated 25-2-2004 passed by the District Judge, Habigonj in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 08 of 2004 staying operation of the order dated 29-1-2004 passed by the Assistant Judge, Madhabpur, in Title Suit No. 72 of 2002 allowing an order of temporary injunction restraining the defendants till disposal of the suit.

<u>2. By this Rule the opposite party No. 1 was called upon to show cause an to why the order impugned in this Rule should not be set aside and such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.</u>

<u>3. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 4 of 1987 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Madhabpur, Habiganj. That suit was decreed ex parte by order dated 8-2-1989 and that decree was made final on 23-11-1995.</u>

<u>4. The present petitioner was not made a party in that suit who filed Title Suit No. 77 of 2002 on 3-8-2002 for setting aside the preliminary decree, and final decree passed in Title Suit No. 4 of 1987 and also for a permanent injunction restraining the present opposite party No. 1 from disturbing the plaintiff's peaceful possession in 0.01-1/4 acre of land appertaining to Plot No. 683 under Khatian No. 297 of mouza Sultanpur Uttar under Police Station Madhabpur, District Habiganj till disposal of the suit. The present petitioner made an application on 3-8-2002 for restraining the opposite-party No. 1 by way of temporary injunction from dispossessing the petitioner from his homestead constructed upon the suit land and from disturbing his peaceful possession in the said homestead and from causing any damage to the said homestead. The learned Assistant judge by order dated 29-1-2004 allowed the prayer for injunction on contest and restrained the present opposite-party as prayed for.</u>

5. Being aggrieved by the said order the present opposite-party has preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 2004 on 25-2-2004. The opposite-party made a prayer for stay of operation of the order dated 29-1-2004 and the learned District Judge, Habiganj by order dated 25-2-2004 stayed operation of the said order till disposal of the Miscellaneous Appeal.

6. Being aggrieved be the said order the present petitioner has moved this Court in Civil Revision No. 1330 of 2004 and this Court by order dated 8-5-2004 stayed operation of the order of stay granted by the learned District Judge, Habiganj dated 25-2-2003 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 2002. After getting the certified copy of this Court's order dated 8-5-2004 the present petitioner submitted an application before the learned Assistant Judge, Madhabpur in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1988 for staying all further proceedings of that execution case till disposal of this Civil Revision and the learned Assistant Judge by order No. 93 dated 15-5-2004 rejected the said application contending, inter alia, that earlier the petitioner made an application for stay of execution case and that was rejected and thereafter he moved before the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4337 of 2002 and the Rule issued in that civil revision was also discharged.

7. Thereafter, the Assistant Judge, Madhabpur, Habiganj proceeded with the Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1988. This petitioner made another application on 17-5-2004 before the executing Court for staying all further proceedings of the said Execution Case but the said application was rejected and the petitioner was evicted on 17-5-04 from his homestead on execution of the decree of Title Suit No. 4 of 1987 vide Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1998 and handed over possession in favour of the present opposite-party No. 1.

8. Thereafter the present petitioner made an application before this Court in Civil Revision No. 1330 of 2004 praying for a mandatory injunction directing the opposite party No. 1 to restore possession in the suit land of Title Suit No. 72 of 2002 and also for demolition of structures raised after taking possession and this Court by order dated 30-6-2004 issued a Rule calling upon the opposite-party No. 1 to show cause as to why the mandatory injunction for restoring the possession of the suit land to the petitioner described in the schedule of which the petitioner was dispossessed by the opposite-party No. 1 during pendency of the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 2004 of the Court of the District Judge, Habiganj, arising out of Title Suit No. 72 of 2002 of the Court of Assistant Judge, Madhabpur, Habiganj should not be passed against the opposite-party No. 1 and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

9. The Civil Revision No. 1330 of 2004 and Civil Rule No. 368(R) of 2004 having arisen out of the same subject matter are taken up for analogous hearing and for disposal of both the Rules.

10. Mr. AB Roy Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submitted that admittedly the petitioner has filed Title Suit No. 72 of 2002 praying for getting the ex parte judgment and decree dated 8-2-1989 passed in Title Suit No. 4 of 1987 set aside and also for setting aside the final decree passed in the said suit and admittedly, the petitioner has obtained an order of ad-interim injunction on contest against the present opposite party No. 1 from disturbing the peaceful possession of the petitioner in 0.01-1/4 acre of land of Plot No. 683, mouza Sultanpur and admitted that order of injunction is continuing. He submitted that the opposite party although obtained an ex parte order of stay of operation of the order dated 29-1-2004 passed in Title Suit No. 72 of 2002 by order dated 25-2-2004 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 2004 but the said order has been stayed by this Court by order dated 8-5-2004. He submitted that by order dated 8-5-2004 the order of temporary injunction granted by the learned Assistant Judge, Madhabpur, dated 29-1-2004 has been restored and has been made operative. He submitted that so long that order stands the opposite party cannot take possession in the suit land on execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 4 of 1987. He submitted that it was the bounden duty of the learned Assistant Judge to maintain status quo till disposal of the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 2004 and also till disposal of the Civil Revision No. 1330 of 2004 pending before this Court. He submitted that the petitioner has been dispossessed from his homestead during subsistence of the order of injunction dated 29-1-2004 and, as such, he is entitled to get restoration of possession under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He submitted that the order dated 25-2-2004 passed by the learned District Judge is absolutely an illegal order in view of the fact that the petitioner has been able to make out a case that he is living in his homestead constructed upon the suit land and he was not made a party in Title Suit No. 4 of 1987. He further submitted that the Title Suit No. 4 of 1987 was filed beyond the knowledge of the present petitioner and that was decreed ex parte. He submitted that the present petitioner having filed a suit for setting aside the ex parte decree and having obtained an order of injunction on contest in restraining the opposite party, the latter was not entitled to get possession in the said land during subsistence of that order. He prayed for a direction to the learned Assistant Judge, Madhabpur for restoration of possession in favour of the petitioner before disposal of the suit and also before disposal of the Miscellaneous, Appeal No. 8 of 2004.

11. Mr Md Zulfikar Ali, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, has submitted that the present petitioner of the Rule being a 3rd party to the decree and also to the execution case was not entitled to get any order of stay of the execution proceedings. He further submitted that previously the present petitioner made an application before the executing Court to stay of all further proceeding of Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1998 and that prayer was rejected and against which they moved before this Court in Civil Revision No. 4337 of 2002 and this Court also rejected the prayer for stay. So long the order stands the petitioner is not entitled to get any restoration of possession in the suit land. He prayed for discharge of the Rule.

12. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties. I have perused the materials on record.

<u>13. It is admitted that the Title Suit No. 4 of 1987 was filed seeking for a preliminary decree for partition without impleading the present petitioner as a party. It is also admitted that the said suit was decreed ex parte and the ex parte decree was made final. It is also admitted that the present opposite-party being the decree holder started Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1998 for getting possession in the decretal land. It is also admitted that the present petitioner has filed Title Suit No. 72 of 2002 and has obtained an ad-interim injunction on contest by order dated 29-1-2004 against the present opposite-party restraining him from disturbing the peaceful possession of the petitioner in the homestead and also from damaging the homestead. It is also admitted that the said injunction order is in force till today. Mr Md Zulfikar Ali, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, has conceded before this Court that the said order is still in existence. Admittedly, the petitioner was in possession in his homestead constructed upon plot No. 683 covering an area of 0.01-1/4 acre. Although the petitioner earlier moved unsuccessfully upto this Court in Civil Revision No. 4337 of 2002 for getting stay of all further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1998 but that Civil Revision arose out of an order of refusing stay in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1998 holding that a 3rd party has no locus standi to stay any execution proceedings. But after getting unsuccessful in the said revision case, the present petitioner has instituted the Title Suit No. 72 of 2002 and has obtained an order of injunction on contest. It is the duty of the Court, who granted injunction, to protect the verdict of the Court. Admittedly, the present petitioner having been in possession was entitled to retain his possession in his homestead till the order of injunction dated 29-1-2004 is set aside. The learned District Judge although granted an order of ad-interim stay against the order dated 29-1-2004 but the said order having been stayed by this Court by order dated 8-5-2004, the learned Assistant Judge was not lawfully entitled to execute the decree. It further appears that the petitioner by submitting a certified copy of this Court's order dated 8-5-2004 prayed for stay of all further proceeding of Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1998 but the said application was rejected. This way the learned Assistant Judge executed the decree disobeying this Court's order dated 8-5-2004. The learned Assistant Judge ought not to have executed the decree violating the order of this Court and ought not to have handed over possession in favour of the opposite party No. 1 who has been restrained by his own order dated 29-1-2004 from disturbing the peaceful possession of the present petitioner and from making any damage to his homestead. It was the duty of learned Assistant Judge to maintain his injunction order dated 29-1-2004 unless that order is disturbed by any superior Court but without doing so he has violated his own order and has violated the order of this Court. It is the consistent view of our Appellate Division that in an appropriate case the Court in exercise of its inherent power can issue a temporary injunction in mandatory form to restore the status quo ante in the suit. This view finds support from the case law of Bakul Kanti Das and others vs Abul Hossain and others, reported in 47 DLR (AD) 6. I find that the said decision in fully applicable in the instant case. I find that there is merit in the Rule issued in Civil Revision No. 1330 of 2004 and also in Civil Rule No. 368(R) of 2004. Mr Md Zulfikar Ali, at this stage, felt it difficult to oppose the Rules.</u>

14. In the result, the Rule issued in Civil Revision No. 1330 of 2004 is made absolute without any order as to costs. The order dated 25-2-2004 passed by the learned District Judge, Habiganj in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 2004 is set aside. The leaned District Judge is directed to hear and dispose of the appeal as early as possible preferably within 3(three) months from the date or receipt of this order. The Rule issued in Civil Rule No. 368(R) of 2004 is also made absolute. The learned Assistant Judge, Madhabpur is directed to restore possession in 0.033 acre of land of Plot No. 683, khatian No. 279, Mouza Sultanpur, Police Station Madhabpur, District Habiganj, in favour of the petitioner within 7(seven) days from the date of receipt of this order. The learned Assistant Judge is also directed to dispose of the suit as early as possible preferably within 1(one) year from the date of receipt of this order.

The learned Assistant Judge is directed to Communicate the compliance of this order to this Court within 15(fifteen) days from the date of receipt of this order by him and also directed to communicate the said order to the learned District Judge, Habiganj.

End.

Doctor J. H. Gazi and others --------- Respondents.
(In C.A. No.49 of 2006
full_judgment:
S.K. Sinha, J: These appeals, by leave, one at the instance of auction purchaser Lt. Col. M.A. Mannan (Retd) and other at the instance of the decree holder Social Investment Bank Limited arise out the same judgment in Writ Petition Nos.4783 of 2003 and 4803 of 2003 and therefore these appeals are disposed of by this judgment analogously.

<u>2. The respondent No. 1 Social Investment Bank Limited instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 58 of 2000 for realization of Tk .1,77,48,652/- against the respondent Nos. 3-5. The suit was ultimately decreed on 28th September, 2001 and pursuant thereto the decree holder put the decree into execution in Title Execution Case No.26 of 2002 on 7th March, 2002 against the judgment debtors for recovery of a sum of Tk. 2,09,59,112/-. There was publication notice for selling of the mortgaged property on auction on 18th February, 2003 and ultimately 12th March, 2003 was fixed for sale of the mortgaged property. As no bidder attended in the auction sale on successive three dates on 12th March, 30th March and 14th June, 2003, the decree holder came up with a application that it had amicably settled the dispute regarding payment of the decreetal amount with the judgment debtor and prayed for staying further proceedings of the executing case and that the judgment debtor had already deposited Tk. 40,00,000/-. The executing Court adjourned the matter on 29th June, 2003 for payment of the balance decreetal amount, failing which, it was directed that the auction sale of the property will be held on that day. On 29th June, the decree holder again filed an application for adjournment of the matter on the ground that the terms of settlement are yet to be settled between the parties. The executing Court rejected the said application and took up the matter for auction sale when the appellant Lt. Col. M.A. Mannan (Retd) submitted tender for Tk. 1,52,00,000/-. The other two bidders being disqualified their tenders were rejected. The executing Court accepted the tender of the appellant and directed him to deposit the balance consideration amount within 10 days. On the same day the decree holder prayed for not accepting in the tender submitted by the appellant M. A. Mannan. The executing Court did not pass any order on the reasoning that the tender of Abdul Mannan had already been accepted.</u>

3. The decree holder thereupon instituted the above Writ Petition No. 4783 of 2003 against the said order dated 29th June, 2003. The judgment-debtor also filed Writ Petition No. 4803 of 2003 challenging the said order of the executing Court. The auction-purchaser, the present appellant contested the writ petitions by filing affidavits-in-opposition contending that the executing Court has committed no error of law in accepting his tender, that there was no compromise between the decree holder and the judgment debtor, that the decree holder in collusion with the judgment debtor filed the application for stay and that the writ petitions are liable to be dismissed.

<u>4. The High Court Division upon hearing the parties made both the rules absolute, quashed the order dated 29th June, 2003 and directed executing Court to proceed with the execution case in accordance with law with a further direction that if any valid compromise is effected between the parties that can be accepted on being satisfied as per provisions of law, and that if no valid compromise is effected, the executing Court will publish fresh notice for sale of the mortgaged property in accordance with law.</u>

<u>5. The High Court Division after reproducing section 33 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 observed that as no bidder participated in the bid on two previous dates, the Adalat on the application of the judgment-debtor adjourned the proceedings and fixed 29th June, 2003 for payment of the rest of the decreetal dues, and the selling of the property without publication or advertisement in the newspaper is not authorised by the law, and that the Adalat had no jurisdiction to sell the property in such manner it sold to the respondent No. 5.</u>

6. It is contended on behalf of the appellant that the High Court Division erred in law in finding that sections 33 and 39 had not been complied with by the executing Court while selling the mortgaged property on 29th June, 2003.

7. Section 33 provides the procedure for selling any property by the Artha Rin Adalat for realization of the decreetal amount. Sub-section (1) of section 33 provides for publication of notice by giving 15 days time inviting tender for auction sale at least in one national daily newspaper. Sub-sections (2) and (3) provide the procedure for filing tender by the intending purchasers. Sub-section (4) of section 33 provides that if it is not practicable to sell the property on auction under sub-sections (1), (2) and (3), the Adalat shall direct publication of notice at least in two Bangali daily newspapers, and if it is practicable in a local newspaper, as per provisions of Sub-section (1) of section 33. These provisions clearly show that at the initial stage the publication of notice for sale of the mortgaged property or any other property be made in a national daily newspaper and on such publication if the sale cannot be effected, then the Adalat will direct for publication of notice for sale at least two daily national newspapers by giving 15 days’ time, which is the minimum requirement of law.

8. In the case in hand, we noticed that by order dated 12th May, 2003 the executing Court fixed 14th June, 2003 for auction sale but on that day no bidder had participated for purchasing the mortgaged property. On the other hand, the decree holder filed application for staying the proceedings on the ground that it had reached at a mutual settlement with the judgment debtor for payment of the decreetal amount. In the context of the matter the executing Court ought to have accepted the prayer. And if such prayer cannot be acceded to, the Court should have directed to publish notice for selling the mortgaged property on auction on 29th June, 2003 but the executing Court without publishing any notice required by law sold the mortgaged property in auction on that day despite the objection raised by the decree-holder on the ground that it had already compromised the dispute with judgment-debtor and that the judgment-debtor had already deposited Tk.40,00,000/- against the decreetal amount. This order of the executing Court is in violation of sub-section (4) of Section 33 of the Artha Rin Adalat.

<u>9. The intention of the legislature i.e. the Artha Rin Adalat Ain is explicit. It encourages amicable settlement of the disputes outside the Court. It is the cardinal rule for construction of Act of Parliament that they should be construed according to the intention expressed in the Acts themselves. In construing Acts of Parliament we are to look not only at the language of the preamble or of any particular clause, but the language of the whole Act. In the Ain, a settlement can be effected at three stages of proceedings; firstly, at the pretrial stage of the proceedings under sections 21 and 22; secondly, after the passing of the decree and during the pendency of execution proceedings under section 38 and the last phase is under section 45, which authrorizes the Artha Rin Adalat to accept the settlement or conciliation for the payment of the decreetal amount at any stage of the proceeding i.e. even at the final stage of the execution proceedings. In this case the decree holder itself is eager to settle up the dispute amicably and accordingly it filed the 1 application for staying further proceedings of the execution case before the auction sale was held, which prayer is normally made by the judgment-debtors. The order-sheet shows that the executing Court is very much interested in putting the property in auction sale despite the objection raised by the decree holder. The Courts are adjudicating a lis in accordance with law but in this case we find the executing Court has adjudicated the matter in such a manner, which can be taken as has been done in accordance with law. If the decree holder is satisfied with the terms of compromise and volunteers that it has compromised the dispute, the Court is left with no option but to accept the prayer and pass necessary order for compromise.</u>

10. According to Dicey, Judges are not allowed to decide a case on the basis of whatever they consider just or fair. They are constrained by 'definite principles of law' and by binding precedent. To avoid an arbitrary discretion in the Courts, Hamilton in the Federalist Papers argued, it is indispensable that they should be bound down by strict rules and precedents which serve to define and point out their duty in every particular case that comes before them. Courts of law are essential to act and assume their role as guardians of the rule of law. It is said that source of judicial power is the law but, in reality, the effective exercise of judicial power originates from two sources; firstly, is the public acceptance of the authority or pronouncement of the judiciary, and secondly, the source is the integrity of the judiciary. The very existence of justice delivery system depends on the judges who, for the time being, constitute the system. The judges have to honour the judicial office which they hold as a public trust. Their every action and their every word-must show and reflect correctly that they hold the office as a public trust. The greatest strength of the judiciary is the faith of the people in it. Faith, confidence and acceptability cannot be commanded; they have to be earned.

11. In the premises, the Artha Rin Adalat has exceeded its jurisdiction in selling the mortgaged property in auction without following the provisions law and that's too when the decree holder itself prayed in Court that it had already compromised the matter with the judgment-debtor subject to the approval of the Bangladesh Bank.

12. We, therefore, find merit in these appeals. Since the appellant Lt. Col. M.A. Mannan (Retd) had deposited Tk. 38,00000/- on 29th June, 2003 against security he should be compensated. Learned Counsel appearing for the judgment debtor contended that the judgment debtor is ready to compensate the auction purchaser. The judgment-debtor, is therefore, directed to pay solatium to the auction purchaser, the appellant, at the rate of 10% interest per annum on the amount deposited by him from the date of deposit within fifteen from the date of receipt of the judgment. We direct the Artha Rin Adalat or the decree holder, as the case may be, to return back the money to the auction purchaser with interest, after realising if from the judgment-debtor within fifteen days from the date of the receipt of the judgment.

13. The appeals are dismissed with the above observations without any order as to costs.

End.

Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner

Vs.
Saudi-Bangladesh Industrial and Agricultural Investment Company limited (SABINCO) and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain, J.:- This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the order dated 11.07.2010 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 later re-numbered as First Appeal No. 25 of 2006 directing the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka to accept deposit of 50% of the decretal amount in cash in Money Suit No.77 of 1994 and to return to the appellant the Bank Guarantee No. DDBL, 120/64/99 dated 04.07.1999 for an amount of Tk. 1,15,99,734.69 issued by Dutch-Bangle Bank Limited and to stay all further proceedings of Artha Execution Case No. 117 of 2009 pending before Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka for a period of 2(two) months from date.

2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in brief, are:

The petitioner herein, State Bank of India as the plaintiff, instituted Money Suit No. 77 of 1994 impleading Saudi-Bangladesh Industrial Investment Company as defendant and obtained a decree. Against the judgment and decree dated 24.04.1999, Saudi-Bangladesh Industrial Investment Company Limited (in short, SBINCO), Dhaka filed F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 which was allowed to be registered by the High Court Division on 11.07.1999. Against the order dated 11.07.1999 of the High Court Division, the State Bank of India, Dhaka Branch, filed a civil petition for leave to appeal in which leave was granted by this Division resulting in the initiation of Civil Appeal No. 203 of 2000. After hearing this Division allowed the appeal setting aside registration of memorandum of appeal in F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999.

3. After a lapse of two years SABINCO (respondent) filed an application in the said non-existent F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 before the High Court Division. The State Bank of India, Dhaka Branch (plaintiff-petitioner), opposed the application on the ground that the said application has been filed in a non-existent F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 later renumbered as F.A. No. 25 of 2006. On 11.07.2010, the High Court Division allowed the application relying on a case reported in 5 ADC (2008)478 holding that "we find the instant application has been brought by the applicant before as under similar circumstance."

4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned order dated 11.07.2010 passed by the High Court Division, the State Bank of India, Dhaka Branch (the plaintiff) as the leave petitioner has filed this instant civil petition for leave to appeal,

5. Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the leave petitioner, submits that the High Court Division passed the impugned order dated 11.07.2010 in F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 renumbered as F. A. No. 25 of 2006, although against the very registration of F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 dated 11.07.1999, the leave petitioner filed a civil .Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 948 of 1999 before this Division in which leave was granted resulting in Civil Appeal No. 203 of 2000 and that the appeal was allowed setting aside the registration of the F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 and as such the High Court Division did not have the jurisdiction to pass the impugned order dated 11.07.2010 and consequently, the impugned judgment should be set aside. He further submits that the High Court Division misconstrued the, judgment in the case of Bombay Sweets & Company Limited vs. President, Appeal Tribunal, Customs, Excise and VAT and another, 5 ADC(2008)478 and as such, the impugned order should be set aside.

6. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that the High Court Division relied upon a finding of the case of Bombay Sweets & Company Limited (ibid), in which it was held "we are inclined to give the petitioner a chance to get the appeal heard on merit by snaking 50% deposit either of the demanded VAT or Penalty imposed on it by respondent No. 2 i.e., the Commissioner of Customs, Excise and VAT, Dhaka South, Dhaka pursuant to the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 42 of the VAT Act as prevalent at the relevant time as has been quoted hereinbefore" and as such, the impugned order should be maintained.

7. We have considered the submissions of the learned Senior Advocates, and perused the impugned order and the materials on record.

8. Before the Artha Rin Adalat respondent No. 1 tendered a bank guarantee to the extent of 50% of the decretal amount and applied for acceptance thereof. The Artha Rin Adalat rejected the application on 05.07.1999 on the ground that the application was filed after expiry of 30 days from the date of the judgment and decree. Respondent No. 1 filed Writ Petition No. 2465 of 1999 impugning the order dated 05.07.1999 of the Artha Rin Adalat. The High Court Division issued a Rule and also passed an interim order allowing respondent No. 1 to file an appeal against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat on the basis of the bank guarantee filed in the Artha Rin Adalat for an amount equivalent to 50% of the decretal amount. Curiously enough, the memorandum of appeal was not registered pursuant to the interim order passed in the writ petition.

9. A Civil Division Bench of the High Court Division, relying on its earlier decision made in F.A.T. No. 358 of 1999 (wrongly written as F.M.A.T. No. 358 of 1949) allowed respondent No. 1 to register the memorandum of F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 by passing the following order:

"The appellants are permitted to file the Memorandum of Appeal with the Bank. Guarantee on the terms and conditions as laid down by this Court on 24,06,1999 in F.M.A.T. No. 358 of 1999. Let the. Memorandum of Appeal be registered, if it is otherwise in order,"

10. The period of 30 days' limitation expired on 13.07.1999 and prior to that respondent No. 1 furnished its bank guarantee on 05.07.1999 as stated above. Against the order dated 11.07.1999 passed in F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999, the leave petitioner filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 984 of 1999 before this Division in which leave was granted resulting in Civil Appeal No. 203 of 2000. This Division by its judgment and order dated 02.06.2008 set aside the order dated 11.07.1999 passed by the High Court Division in F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 permitting respondent No.1 to register the memorandum of appeal against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Money Suit No. 77 or 1994 with a bank guarantee for an amount equivalent to 50% of the decretal amount. Respondent No.1 filed Civil Review Petition No. 34 of 2004 before this Division against the judgment and order dated 02.06.2008, but the review petition was also dismissed on 21.03.2010. Later, the leave petitioner filed Artha Jari Case No. 111 of 2009. On 25.05.2010, despondent No. 1 filed application in F.A. No. 25 of 2006 (arising out of F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999) for direction upon the Artha Rin Adalat to accept 50% of the decretal amount and to return the bank guarantee and also to stay all further proceedings of Artha Jari Case No.117 of 2009. On 11.07.2010, the High Court Division allowed the application on contest and directed the Artha Rin Adalat to accept the 50% of the decretal amount in casts and directed to return the bank guarantee to respondent No. 1 and also stayed all further proceedings of Anita Jail Case No. 117 of 2009. On 30.09.2010, respondent No. 1 complied with the order of the High Court Division dated 11.07.2010 by depositing 50% of the decretal amount with the Artha Rin Adalat by a pay order dated 03.09.2010. On 10.10.2010, the leave petitioner has filed this civil petition for leave to appeal against the impugned order dated 11.07.2010 and obtained the order of stay on 11.07.2010.

11. Admittedly by the order dated 11.07.2010, the High Court Division allowed the application filed by respondent No. 1 and directed the Artha Rin Adalat to accept 50% of the decretal amount in cash and to return bank guarantee and to stay all further proceedings of Artha Jari Case No. 117 of 2009.

12. There is no scope to pass the order dated 11.07.2010 when this Division in Civil Appeal No. 203 of 2000 set aside the order dated 11.07.1999 passed by the High Court. Division in F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 permitting respondent No. 1 to register its memorandum of appeal against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Money Suit No. 77 of 1994 with the bank guarantee for an amount equivalent to 50% of the decretal amount. The impugned order dated 10.07.2010 was passed in F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 renumbered as F.A. No. 25 of 2006 when there was no existence either of F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 or F.A. No. 25 of 2006 in view of the judgment delivered by this Division passed in Civil Appeal No. 203 of 2000 dated 02.06.2008. The reason for filing an application in a dead F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 renumbered as F.A. No. 25 of 2006 is not comprehensible. Even the High Court Division could not detect that there was no scope for passing the impugned order dated 11 07.2010.

13. The High Court Division mainly relied upon the case of Bombay Sweets & Company Limited (ibid) while passing the impugned order. It is pertinent to quote the portion of the judgment relied upon by the High Court Division as well as by Mr. Mahmudul Islam which is as under:

"We are inclined to give the petitioner a chance to get the appeal heard on merit by snaking 50% deposit either of the demanded VAT or Penalty imposed on it by respondent No. 2 i.e., the Commissioner of Customs, Excise and VAT, Dhaka South, Dhaka pursuant to the provisions of subsection 2 of section 42 of the VAT Act as prevalent at the relevant time as has been quoted hereinbefore."

14. The quoted portion of the judgment is a finding of the high Court Division, approved by this Division.

15. Having gone through the entire judgment, in general and paragraph-5 thereof, in particular, we find that in paragraph-5, the salient findings of the High Court Division, were quoted within inverted commas. The leave petitioner of the aforesaid reported judgment challenged the judgment of the High Court Division so tar as it related to the operative portion thereof in which the High Court Division directed the leave petitioner to deposit either 50% of the demanded VAT or the Penalty pursuant to the order passed by respondent No. 2 on 25.11.1996 within 3 months. In the aforesaid reported case, it was observed that there was no justification or ground for filing the civil petition for leave to appeal impugning the judgment of the High Court Division. This Divisions however, observed that the findings made by the High Court Division were legally sound and did not call for any interference. Though this Division approved of the findings of the high Court Division in the case of Bombay Sweets & Company Llimited (ibid), we find that there is no scope to rely upon the above quoted finding by Mr. Mahmudul Islam as being contrary to the provision of section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalt Ain, 1990. Section 7 provides in no uncertain terms that the appeal shall have to be filed within 30 days of the pronouncement of the judgment and decree and that at least 50% of the decretal amount must be deposited in the Artha Rain Adalat Which passed the decree.

16. In the case of JMS Glass Industries Ltd vs. Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal and others (2012) 64 DLR (AD) 43 which is almost identical  in respect of facts of Bombay Sweets & Company Limited (ibid), this Division has held that in order to file an appeal under section 42 of Value Added Tax Act (XXII of 1991)the percentage of the demanded VAT and/or penalty must be deposited at the time of filing the appeal and in the absence of such deposit an appeal cannot be accepted. The principle laid down in JMS Glass Industries Ltd. (ibid) reveals that this Division speaks of filing an appeal under section 42 of Value Added Tax Act by depositing the required amount, and not by furnishing bank guarantee.

17. Section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990 is quoted below:

“৭। আপীল।-(১) কোন ব্যক্তি অর্থ ঋণ আদালতের কোন রায় বা ডিক্রি দ্বারা ক্ষুব্ধ হইলে তিনি উক্ত রায় বা ডিক্রি প্রদানের তারিখ হইতে ৩০ দিনের মধ্যে হাইকোর্ট বিভাগে আপীল করিতে পারিবেনঃ

তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, অর্থ ঋণ আদালতের কোন অন্তর্বর্তী আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে কোন আপীল দায়ের করা যাইবে না।

(২) কোন বিবাদী কোন ডিক্রির বিরুদ্ধে আপীল দায়ের করিতে ইচ্ছুক হইলে তিনি তাঁহার বিরুদ্ধে ডিক্রিকৃত অর্থের অন্ততঃ অর্ধেক অর্থ ডিক্রি প্রদানকারী আদালতের নিকট জমা করিয়া আপীল দায়ের করিতে পারিবেন এবং উক্ত অর্থ জমা না করিলে তাঁহার আপীল গ্রহণযোগ্য হইবে না।

18. The section quoted above manifests that a person aggrieved by a judgment or decree-of the Artha Rin Adalat shall have to file the appeal within 30 days front the date of the judgment or decree, as the case may be, and that any defendant can file appeal against the decree by depositing 50% of the decretal amount in Court which passed the decree.

19. It is a truism that Artha Rin Adalat Ain,1990 (since repealed) is a special law and there is no scope for entertaining an appeal against the judgment of the Artha Rin Adalat beyond the period of limitation and also without depositing 50% of the decretal amount within 30 days from the date of the decree.

20. In this connection, reliance may be made on the case of Abdus Sattar and others vs. International Finance and Investment Commerce Limited, 21 BLD. (AD)77, in which, this Division in para-6 of the judgment held as under:

"6. Section 7(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain,1990 provides that within 30 days from the date of making the decree the appeal is to be filed before the High Court Division and sub-section (2) of section 7 provides that no appeal shall be entertained unless half of the decretal amount is deposited in the Court making the decree in the suit. Thus, section 7 prescribes two conditions to be satisfied by an appellant one the anneal must be preferred within 30 days from the date of the decree and the other, no appeal shall be entertained unless half of the decretal amounts deposited in the Court making the decree Section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain,1990 no-where speaks about bank guarantee. The, expression A_C used in sub-section (2) of section 7 of the Act cannot be construed to be "bank guarantee". The expression artha means (A_C) as used in this sub-section is equivalent in English cash money and not "Bank Guarantee". At the time of tendering the Memorandum of Appeal before the High Court Division the appellant did not deposit half of the decretal amount in the trial Court, Nowhere in section 7 it is provided that such deposit beyond the period of 30 days' from the date of decree in compliance with the requirement of section 7 for the purpose of entertainment a Memorandum of Appeal. Even, on the event of granting time by the High Court Division for depositing, the some as contended by the learned Advocate of the petitioner, the deposit in the instant case not having been made within the statutory time cannot be construed to be a valid deposit for entertainment of a Memorandum of Appeal."(emphasis added)

21. The judgment referred to above reveals that there’s no scope for filing of an appeal after 30 days from the date of pronouncement of the judgment and decree of Artha Adalat and that 50% of the decretal amount must be deposited within that period in the Court which passed the decree. But in the case in hand, the appeal was filed with a bank guarantee of 50% of the decretal amount. Pursuant to the impugned order dated 11.07.2010, respondent No. 1 deposited 50% of the decretal amount after many years of passing of the decree. Such a deposit after expiry of limitation cannot be taken as valid deposit made in a dead F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 renumbered as F.A. No. 25 of 2006.

22. Such being the case, F.A.T. No. 511 of 1999 renumbered as F.A. No. 25 of 2006 was incompetent from its very inception because of limitation and not depositing 50% of the decretal amount within that period. In view of the discussion made before, the quoted finding of Bombay Sweets & Company Limited (ibid) being wrong has no manner of application to the facts and circumstances of the present case.

<u>23. What is important to note here is that how the High Court Division could pass the impugned order permitting respondent No. 1 to deposit 50% of the decretal amount long after the special period of limitation of thirty days provided for by the Artha Rin Ain, 1990 is not comprehensible. The High Court Division can not legislate something which is not in the statute itself. In his "The Nature of the Judicial Process", Justice Benjamin Cardozo of the U.S. Supreme Court stated "No doubt the limits for the judges are narrower. He legislates only between gaps. He fills the open spaces in the law." What Justice Benjamin Carded tries to mean is that if anything is missing in the law, the Court can supply that. In the case in hand, there is no gap in section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and as such, it cannot be said that an appeal against the judgment or decree of the Artha Rin Adalat could be entertained beyond 30 days' period of limitation and also without deposit of 50% of the decretal amount.</u>

<u>24. Considering the chequered history of the case and also the sufferings of both the sides, we are not inclined to grant leave. It would be better to set at rest the protected litigation at this stage. Therefore, we have decided to dispose of the civil petition for leave to appeal setting aside the impugned order passed by the High Court Division.</u>

25. Accordingly, this civil petition for leave to appeal is disposed of and the impugned order dated 11.07.2010 it hereby set aside.

End.
