full_judgment:
S.K. Sinha, J: Appellants obtained leave from this Court from the judgment and order dated 13th May, 2003 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 6768 of 2001.

2. Short facts relevant for the disposal of the appeal are that one Chand Mia, predecessor-in-interest of the appellants, instituted Title Suit No.53 of 1990 in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge seeking rectification of a deed and declaration of title in respect of the third schedule land claiming that he was the owner of the suit land on the basis of four deeds and the Khatian was also prepared in his name. Subsequently, he sold the second schedule land measuring an area of 0028 decimals to the defendants by registered kabala dated 10th December, 1965. Thereafter, the defendants attempted to encroach into the plaintiffs land when they disclosed that they had purchased the suit land measuring 05 decimals by the said deed. The plaintiff thereupon obtained a copy of the deed and came to know that the defendants fraudulently included 03 decimals more land in the schedule of the deed although he sold only 0028 decimals. He claimed that he did not sell 05 decimals of land to the defendants and that the deed so far as it relates to the excess area of land was forged, which was required to be rectified.

3. The defendants contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and claimed that the plaintiff sold 05 decimals of land for valuable consideration and that the pursuant to the deed he delivered possession of the suit land. The suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The trial Court dismissed the suit. On appeal by the plaintiff being Title Appeal No.97 of 1996, the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Sylhet who heard the said appeal reversed the judgment of the trial Court and decreed the suit. The Single Bench of the High Court Division, however, in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction against the said judgment and order of the Court of appeal below, set aside the judgment of the Court of appeal below and restored those of the trial Court. In the plaint the plaintiff sought the following reliefs:

“(ক) বাদী কর্তৃক বিবাদীগন বরাবরে বিগত ১০/১২/৬৫ খৃঃ মোতাবেক ১৩৭২ সনের ২৪শে অগ্রহায়ন তারিখের রেজিষ্টারীযুক্ত ১৯৬৬ খৃঃ সনের ৮৮৪ নং দলিলের তপশীলেবর্ণিত ৫ পাঁচ শতক (নিম্ন ১ম তপশীলে যাহা বিষদ ভাবে বর্ণিত) ভূমির স্থল নিম্ন ২য় তপশীলে বর্ণিত .০০২৮ শতক সন্নিবেশিত হইয়াই উল্লেখিত দলিলটি সংশোধন হওয়ার মর্মে ডিক্রি দিতে বিহিতাদেশ হয়।

(খ) নিম্ন ৩য় তপশীলে বর্ণিত ভূমিতে বাদীর স্বত্ব ঘোষনার ডিক্রি দিতে ও বিহিতাদেশ হয়।

(গ) বিবাদীগনের নিম্ন ২য় তপশীলে বর্ণিত ভূমির উপর থাকা গৃহটি বাদীর স্বত্ব দখলীয় নিম্ন ৩য় তপশীলে বর্ণিত ভূমিতে সম্প্রসারন করিতে না পারেন তৎমর্মে বিবাদীগনকে স্থায়ী নিষেধাজ্ঞা দ্বারা বারিত করিয়া ডিক্রি প্রদান করিতে বিহিতাদেশ হয়।”

<u>5. According to the plaintiff he sold 0028 decimals of land but the defendants fraudulently included 003 decimals of land in the impugned deed in collusion with the scribe. The plaintiff did not deny the execution of the disputed deed. Besides claiming title, the plaintiff sought for rectification of the impugned deed under section 31 of the Specific Relief Act. The Court of appeal below as well as the High Court Division totally confused as to the nature of the suit the plaintiff was required to file for the relief. The Court of appeal below was of the view that the plaintiff was entitled to a relief under section 31 and accordingly decreed the suit. The High Court Division, on the other hand, is of the opinion that the suit for rectification of the deed is maintainable subject to the condition that the plaintiff is required to prove that the instrument was obtained through fraud or by mutual mistake of the parties. The plaintiff did not seek for cancellation of the entire deed, and under such circumstances, it was incumbent for him to seek the relief under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, praying for a declaration that the deed in Question so far as it relates to inclusion of 0028 decimals of land is void.</u>

<u>6. Section 31 provides as to when an instrument may be rectified. It is said, through fraud or mutual mistake of the parties an instrument in writing does not truly express their intention, either party, may institute a suit to have the instrument rectified, and if the Court finds it clearly proved that there has been fraud or mistake in framing the instrument, it may rectify the instrument.</u>

<u>7. To establish a case of rectification of an instrument, it is required to prove that there has been either fraud or common mistake. The plaintiff does not claim that 05 decimals of land have been mentioned in the deed due to common mistake or through inadvertence. In case of the rectification of a deed, the Court will amend the language of the instrument for the purpose of making it accord with the true intention of the parties, having ascertained what that intention was. In most cases of rectification, the proximate origin of mistake lies in the carelessness or want of skill of the draftsman, but if, one of the parties to conceal some fact does not wish to disclose that has caused the instrument to be so framed as to defeat the intention known to himself, the cases of this kind are likely to be on the verge of fraud. Therefore, in case of rectification of an instrument it must be proved that it was through a mutual mistake of the parties that instrument in question did not truly express the intention of the parties and the Court is required to see that there has been mistake in framing the instrument and also ascertain the real intention of the parties executing it. If these two elements are satisfied, it is in the discretion of Court to grant rectification.</u>

8. To adjudge a deed as has been created by practicing fraud, the plaint should have been drawn in accordance with Order 6 Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Fraud being an objective fact known the party alleging it, particulars of it must be given. A party alleging undue influence and collusion must also give particulars thereof in the pleading. So also in regard to breach of trust undue influence or misrepresentation. General allegations however strong are insufficient even to amount to an averment of fraud of which any Court will take notice. When a plaintiff is taking a plea of fraud must specifically plead and prove the same. Although 'undue influence' 'fraud' 'misrepresentation' are cognate vices may, in part, overlap in some cases, they are in law distinct categories, and are in view of Order 6 Rule 4 read with Order 6 Rule 2 required to be separately pleaded, with specificity, particularity and precision. It must be remembered that the plaint is the foundation of the suit and it should be drawn up in accordance with law for getting full relief. The plaint is totally silent in this regard.

9. In case of cancellation of an instrument, three conditions are requisite for the exercise of jurisdiction: (i) the instrument is void or voidable against the plaintiff (ii) the plaintiff may reasonably apprehend serious injury by the instrument being left outstanding and (iii) in the circumstances of the case the Court considers it proper to grant relief of preventive justice. Relief as to cancellation of instrument is founded upon  administration of protective justice for fear that the instrument may be vexatiously or injuriously used by the defendant against the plaintiff when the evidence to impeach it may be lost. When the plaintiff seeks to establish title in himself and cannot establish that title without removing insuperable obstruction such as, an instrument to which he has been party, then he must get that the instrument cancelled and his suit is for cancellation of the instrument.

10. The Court of appeal below accepted the argument of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff that it was not a believable story that the plaintiff sold .05 acre of land in Sylhet Municipality area at a consideration of Tk. 95, that the findings of the trial Court regarding the price of the suit land was not acceptable and that since the plaintiff proved his title by adducing documentary evidence, he was not required to prove title by oral evidence. These observations are based on hypothesis, firstly, because the plaintiff failed to prove by adducing documentary evidence that the price of .05 acre of land during the relevant time was much higher, secondly, when the recitals in the admitted deed clearly disclosed the price of the land sold at Tk. 95/- oral evidence varying the recitals in the deed is not admissible and thirdly, the appellate Court declared tie plaintiffs title of the suit land relying on documentary evidence without ascertaining possession in failing to consider that the plaintiff being the original owner it was natural that he had in his possession the original deeds of title but the crux of the matter was whether the defendants got possession of the land covered by the Impugned deed and whether the deed was acted upon. The trial Court on assessment of the evidence came to a definite finding that the defendants are in possession since the date of execution of the deed on 10th December, 1965, so the deed has acted upon. The appellate Court did not reverse the finding of possession.

11. The Court of appeal below failed to notice that when the terms of any contract, grant or other disposition of property, or of any matter required by law to be reduced to the form of a document, have been proved by the production of the document, evidence of any oral statement shall not be given for contradicting, varying, adding to or subtracting from, the terms of the document. In view above, the High Court Division is perfectly justified in holding that there is no ambiguity with respect to the area of land transferred by the deed 10th December, 1965. The High Court Division observed that the plaintiff did not produce any evidence to prove that the defendants in collusion with the scribe included excess area of land in the deed, that the plaintiff has failed to prove that the defendants have obtained the deed by practicing fraud and that he has not produced legal evidence to ascertain the real intention of parties in executing the disputed deed.

12. The High Court Division further held that there was no assertion in the plaint with regard to fraud or mutual mistake of the parties in filing the deed in question, and it is also not available what was the real intention of the parties in executing the deed .The High Court Division made a cursory glance of the oral evidence of the parties and came to the conclusion that the defendants are in possession of the suit land by constructing house for about thirty years. The High Court Division also held that the lower appellate Court did not reverse the findings of possession arrived at by the trial Court. The High Court Division also perused the disputed deed, exhibit 4, and arrived at the finding that the plaintiffs in fact transferred 05 decimals of land by deed dated 10th December, 1965 and that the plaintiff failed to prove that he had really transferred 0028 decimals of land.

13. Learned Counsel appearing for the plaintiff-respondent No.1 failed to repel any of the findings arrived at by the High Court Division. We find that the High Court Division has committed no error of law in interfering with the judgment of the Court of appeal below. We find no ground to interfere with the same.

14. The appeal is, therefore, dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.

parties:
Ibn Sina Trust ------ Petitioner 
Vs 
Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd and anr ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md Arayesuddin J: This Rule was issued calling upon opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 1-4-2004 by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 105 of 2004 rejecting an application under Order XXI, rule 29 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceedings of Money Execution Case No. 89 of 2003 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat, Court, No. 3 Dhaka regarding auction sale of the petitioner's property till disposal of Title Suit No. 105 of 2004 should not be set aside.

2. Relevant fact to dispose of the Rule, in brief, is that the petitioner is a Charitable Organisation registered under the Societies Act, 1982 having good reputation and countrywide name and fame. The petitioner organisation claims to be the lawful owner of the suit property. They did not take any loan from the opposite party Bank. They are not also a guarantor for the money borrowed from the Bank. Yet the opposite party Bank obtained a decree for realisation of the loan money, availed and enjoyed by the opposite party No. 2. In the impugned suit petitioner was imploaded as defendant No. 4. The summons and notice were suppressed and playing fraud upon the Court as well as the parties plaintiff-opposite party No.1 obtained the impugned judgment and decree. Petitioner had no relief under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure as they are not third party. No relief can also be claimed by filing Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code since the suit has been dismissed ex-parte against the petitioner. Therefore, the petitioner was compelled to file a separate suit being Title Suit No. 105 of 2004 in the Court of the Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka challenging the fraudulent decree in view of the decision passed in CPLA No. 572 of 1994 reported in 1995 BLD (AD) 35. In this suit petitioner filed a petition under Order XXI, rule 29 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for stay of all further proceeding of the Artha Jari Case No. 89 of 2003 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 3. Dhaka regarding the auction sale of the petitioner's property till disposal of Title Suit No. 105 of 2004 which was rejected by the Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka on 1-4-2004 in Title Suit No. 105 of 2004. Being aggrieved, petitioner moved this Court in revisional Jurisdiction and obtained the Rule.

3. The Rule has been opposed by opposite party No. 1 by filing affidavit-in-opposition.

4. On behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner, the learned Advocate Mr Enayet Hossain Khan submitted the petitioner is a reputed welfare trust extending medical help to the general public throughout the country and they had no need of money to solicit any loan from the Bank. The petitioner purchased the suit land in 1986. At the time of purchase their vendor did not supply the original deed on the plea that it was lost. The petitioner believed the vendor. Petitioner is in possession of the suit land. But subsequently, their vendor, by suppressing the fact of the alleged transfer took loan from the bank by mortgaging the suit property on deposit of the 'title deed. The Bank, without making any further enquiry about the title and possession, allowed the loan by keeping the original deed. The vendor became a defaulter. As a result Bank filed Title Suit No. 116 of 1998 for realisation of the loan money. In the suit petitioner was made defendant No. 4. But the Bank in collusion with the borrower suppressed all the summons and notices and obtained ex-parte decree against this petitioner. But contested decree was passed against the borrower. The Bank put the decree in execution by filing Money Execution Case No. 89 of 2003. In the judgment the trial Court observed that the borrower has no title in the other lands. So, the land possessed by the petitioner measuring 17 decimals has been put to auction. At the time the petitioner came to know of the impugned judgment and decree. In the meantime the perfod of limitation for filing Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was over. He submitted that finding no other alternative petitioner instituted a separate suit as per decision of the Appellate Division and filed a petition under Order XXI, rule 29 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying the further proceeding of the Money Execution Case No. 89 of 2003. The learned trial Court without considering the petition on merit rejected the same which is not tenable in law. He has further submitted that the trial Court ought to have passed the order of stay till disposal of the suit. To strengthen his argument the learned Advocate submitted that if the suit of the petitioner is decreed and in the meantime he is dispossessed from the suit land there would be further litigation and the very purpose of the suit will be frustrated. The learned Advocate submitted that honorable Appellate Division has categorically opined that the allegation of non-service of summons in a suit of Artha Rin Adalat can be challenged by filing separate suit.

5. On behalf of the opposite party No.1, Mr Morshed Ahmed Khan, the learned Advocate submitted that there is no illegality in the impugned order complained of. He has submitted that petitioner wilfully did not contest the suit. He had sufficient relief in the suit of the Artha Rin Adalat. To elucidate his argument the learned Advocate submitted that the suit has been decreed ex parte against him. So, the proper forum for the petitioner was to file a Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure which is not barred till today if he can prove that he was not aware of the impugned judgment and decree and he acquired knowledge on a certain date. He has further submitted that provision of the Code of Civil Procedure is applicable in the case of Artha Rin Adalat if it is not contrary to the provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. Further submitted, that in section 57, Artha Rin Adalat has been vested with inherent power to grant any relief to the aggrieved party. The learned Advocate submitted that there were sufficient forums before the petitioner to have his remedies in the Artha Rin Adalat, instead of that he has filed a separate suit and prayed for stay of the execution case in that suit. He has submitted that both the courts are of equal power and jurisdiction. In such circumstances the court of the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka had nothing to do with the execution case of the Artha Rin Adalat which has been established by a separate statute. The learned Advocate for the opposite party No.1 submitted that there is no merit in the Rule as there are forums still today open before the petitioner in the Artha Rin Adalat.

<u>6. We have perused the petition, the Rule and the counter-affidavit and heard the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides. It is admitted that the petitioner was defendant No. 4 in Title Suit No. 116 of 1998. Petitioner's contention is that he did not receive any summons and notices of that suit. So he could not contest. His further allegation is that plaintiff and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 collusively suppressed the summons by practicing fraud upon the court. We have perused the judgment of our honorable Appellate Division delivered in CPLA No. 572 of 1994 in the case of Md Mozammel Hoque vs Sonali Bank and another. In that judgment the Appellate Division has given the exhaustive guideline in para 3 which runs as follows:</u>

<u>3. "In the facts and circumstances of the case, if the petitioner's allegation of no service of summons of the suit is correct his remedy of a separate suit is not barred provided his remedy lies under the Artha Rin Adalat Act stood barred at the time of the filing of the suit for no fault of his own. But these are matters of evidence and until the plaintiff petitioner proves these allegations in the suit the decree holder respondent Bank cannot be denied the fruit of its decree for an indefinite period."</u>

<u>With this exhaustive findings their Lordships of the Appellate Division was pleased to dismiss the petition for leave to appeal. In the above findings a clear guideline has been given. A separate suit is not barred provided his remedies under the Artha Rin Adalat Act stood barred at the time of filing of the suit for no fault of his own. Annexure A is the judgment of Title Suit No. 116 of 1998. The suit has been decreed in preliminary form against defendant Nos. 1-2 and 3 and dismissed ex-parte against defendant Nos. 3-4. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that he cannot claim any relief before the Artha Rin Adalat. We are unable to accept this submission in view of the application of the Code of Civil Procedure in the Artha Rin Adalat, Act, 1990 under which the suit Was filed. Section 5(4) of the Act is clear to the effect. Therefore, we find that the door of the Code of Civil Procedure is still' open to the petitioner if he can prove that no summons of notices were served upon him and he had no knowledge of the suit. The learned Advocate submitted that petitioner has no scope to file Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure as the suit has been dismissed ex parte against him. The definition of decree has been misconceived. The leaned Advocate for opposite party No. 1 also admits that petitioner can seek his relief under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure if he can over come limitation.</u>

7. In that view of the matter and the decision of the Honorable Appellate Division passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 572 of 1994 reported in 1995 BLD (AD) 35 we find no merit in the Rule.

Accordingly, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The order of stay passed at the time of the issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated.

End.

vs

full_judgment:
By this Rule the opposite party No.1 was called upon to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 27-6-2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal in Title Appeal No. 165 of 1995 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 28-8-1995 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Barisal, in Title Suit No. 36 of 1994 dismissing the suit should not be set aside, and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and, proper.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 153 of 1988 praying for a declaration of title in the suit land as described in Ka schedule land to the plaint. That suit was transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Barisal and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 36 of 1994. The plaint's case was, inter alia, that the Ka schedule land belonged to Hamejuddin and others. Hatem Ali died leaving behind two daughters Garibjan Bibi and Fatejan Bibi and a son Aptar Ali. The suit land was diluviated into the river in the year, 1934 and reappeared after 15 years i.e. before the Part V of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into being. The revisional survey took place in the year, 1940-42 and, as a result, the RS Khatians were published showing the property to be diluviated. Hamejuddin and Sadat Ali sold their entire share on 12-5-66 in favour of the petitioner Nos. 1-2 and 5-6 and Aptar sold his share to petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 on 5-10-56. Recorded tenant Aminuddin sold his share to petitioner Nos. 1, 2 and 4 on 24-2-68 and delivered possession thereof. Aptar Ali and Garibjan sold their share on 25-5-68 to petitioner Nos. 1-3. This way the petitioners have been in possession in the suit land by constructing their homestead. The defendant opposite parties had no title and possession in the suit land who taking advantage of a note in the record of rights as diluviated land; the concerned Tahshilder claimed the suit property by the first week of Polish 1395 BS and, as such, the suit.

3. The opposite party No.1, being defendant, contested the suit by filing a Written Statement contending, inter alia, that the suit property remained under water for more than 20 years and the title of the plaintiff had ceased to exist and the property was vested absolutely with the Government.

4. It is the further case of the Government that the suit property had been leased out with the landless people and those landless people had been in possession in the suit property.

5. The trial Court framed appropriate issues in the suit and both the parties led evidence.

6. Upon consideration of the evidence on record, the trial Court dismissed the suit by the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-8-1995 against which the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 165 of 1995. The said appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 27-6-2000 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment of the trial Court.

7. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the plaintiffs have obtained the instant Rule.

8. Mr Swapan Kumar Dutta, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, on appearing before this Court, submitted that admittedly the plaintiffs' predecessor was the owner and possessor in the suit property and that property was diluviated in 1934 and reappeared after 15 years. He submitted that the RS operation was held between 1940 and 42. And at that time the property was under water and, as a result, the SA Khatian and the map was prepared having a note as "Shikasti" as diluviated. He submitted that the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into operation after the land had reappeared and the President's Order No. 135 of 1972 has got no manner of application. He submitted that the Courts below utterly failed to consider this aspect judicially. He submitted for an interference by this Court.

9. Mr Md Ferozur Rahman, the learned Assistant Attorney-General, on appearing for the opposite parties, submitted that the property was under water. He submitted that the evidence on record supported that the suit property came within the mischief of President's Order No. 135 of 1972. He further submitted that the Courts below upon consideration of the evidence on record lawfully dismissed the plaintiffs' suit. He further submitted that the plaintiffs, in the revisional application, could not make out any case of non-consideration of any evidence or non-reading of any evidence or misreading of any evidence on record and finally, submitted that there is nothing to interfere by this Court in revision against the concurrent finding of facts arrived at by both the Courts below.

10. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties and have considered their submissions.

<u>11. On perusal of the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court it appears that the plaintiff has sought for declaration of title in a part of a number of plots without specifying the area. The trial Court upon consideration of the evidence on record found the plaintiffs to be out of possession and the appellate Court affirmed the said finding. Mr Swapan Kumar Dutta could not point out from the evidence on record that any evidence is available to support the plaintiffs' possession in the suit. Moreover, the suit land having not been specified and having not been abutted and bounded, a suit for declaration of title is barred under the proviso of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and also under Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Mr Md Firozur Rahman, the learned Assistant Attorney-General relied upon two decisions of our Appellate Division reported in 41 DLR (AD) 141 and / BLC (AD) 26. Upon consideration of the evidence on record and the judgments of the Courts below, it appears that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and the plaintiff ought to have come up with properly instituted suit seeking for consequential relief. I find no merit in the Rule.</u>

12. In the result, the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 27-6-2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal in Title Appeal No. 165 of 1995 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 28-8-1995 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Barisal, in Title Suit No. 36 of 1994 is hereby affirmed.

Send down the lower Court's record at once.

End.

parties:

Vs.
Alifa Khatun and Others (In C.P.No.1265 of 2009)
Nurer Nabi and Others (In C.P.No.1266 of 2009)
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman, J.: These two leave petitions arose out of Title Suit No.73 of 1997 filed in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Feni, seeking declaration that the judgment and decree obtained by the plaintiff of Title Suit No.16 of 1985 is collusive, ineffective and void and not binding upon the plaintiff of the suit and also for partition. The suit was dismissed by the judgment and decree dated 14.09.2000 against which Title Appeal No.121 of 2000 was preferred in the Court of District Judge, Feni, which on transfer was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Feni, dismissing the appeal vide judgment and decree dated 18.09.2006 and being aggrieved there-against the plaintiff preferred Civil Revision No.4698 of 2006 and the defendant also filed another revision case being Civil Revision No.4699 of 2006 and both the Rules issued in the revision cases were heard and disposed of by the impugned judgment and order dated 14.05.2009 making the Rules absolute setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the Courts below with an order for sending back the case to the appellate Court below on remand for fresh hearing having regard to the observations made by the High Court Division.

2. The plaintiffs' case, in short, is that Ahammad Ali and Torab Ali were the original owners of 90 decimals of land in Khatian No.59, which was auction-purchased by Zamindar Babu Sotish Charan Laha, from whom Ayesha Khatun took settlement vide kabuliyat dated 07.11.1945 and on the same date she sold 21 decimals of land to Ohider Rahman and Abul Bashar and the remaining 69 decimals were transferred to her son Gura Mia and the sons of first wife of Torab Ali, and delivered possession thereof. The plaintiffs purchased land from the rightful owners which has been detailed in schedule `Kha' in the plaint. The plaintiff of Title Suit No.16 of 1985 obtained a decree dated 29.04.1987 without serving any notice upon the plaintiff Nos.1-3 and without impleading plaintiff No.4. The plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land. The defendant No.13 who was plaintiff in Title Suit No.16 of 1985 though has no possession but on the basis of the aforesaid collusive decree claiming title in the suit land and hence the plaintiff after obtaining the decree passed in aforesaid Title Suit No.16 of 1985 filed the instant suit.

3. The defendant No.13 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the plaintiffs' case and contending that his mother Aysha Khatun was the owner of the suit land which he has inherited and is possessing but the plaintiff and other defendants dispossessed him from the suit land for which he filed Title Suit No.16 of 1985 and got the decree in due course within knowledge of the plaintiffs and other defendants.

4. The defendant Nos.1-3, 6, 7, 20, 21 and 24 jointly prayed for their respective sahams by filing an application admitting the plaint case and claiming to have inherited 3.15 decimals of land owned by Ohider Rahman, the defendant Nos.1 and 2 sold 3 decimals of land to defendant No.20 on 15.01.1974 and defendant No.24 purchased land from son of Abdul Khaleque who purchased 9 decimals of land from Saidur Rahman. Defendant Nos.10 and 11 two sisters inherited 4.83 decimals of land along with their three brothers being legal heirs of Saidur Rahman. The defendant No.12 inherited shares of Foyezunessa and defendant No.21 purchased one decimal of land from Abdul Hakim and the defendant Nos.8 and 9 along with Bodu Mia inherited 15 decimals of land as legal heir of Abdul Hakim and the plaintiff No.4  purchased 1½  decimals of land from Bodu Mia. The defendant Nos.3-7 being legal heirs inherited land of Bodu Mia and thus the aforesaid defendant Nos.1-3, 6,7,20,21 and 24 became owner-possessors of 26 decimals and 7.25 decimals of land for which they prayed saham. The defendant Nos. 4,5,14,15 and 20 also prayed for saham by filing an application claiming owner-possessors of 20.25 decimals of land by way of inheritance and purchase. The defendant Nos.16-19 prayed for saham for 4.25 decimals of land claiming ownership and possession through inheritance from the lawful owners.

5. The plaintiffs examined three witnesses and the defendant No.13 examined two witnesses. The defendant Nos.1- 3,6,7,20,21 and 24 examined one witness, the defendant Nos. 4,5,14,15 and 22 examined one witness and the defendant Nos.16- 19 examined one witness in support of their respective claims. The parties also filed documents marked exhibits.

6. The High Court Division appears to have discussed the evidence on record in detail and made the rule absolute setting aside the decree passed by the Courts below and remanded the case for decision by the appellate court below on fresh hearing observing amongst others that:

"Admittedly in the present suit the processes server of summons of Title Suit No.16 of 1985 was not examined as a witness in order to prove that summons was duly served on the defendants (present plaintiffs) and that the process server was a materials witness in the present case, but both the parties did not take any step for examining the concerned process server or to prove the report of the processes server of summons of that suit. This is a material omission on the part of the parties because when the present plaintiffs as defendants of the earlier suit being Title Suit No.16 of 1985 claimed that on summons of that suit was served on them it was the duty of the present contesting defendant No.13 to call for the records of Title Suit No.16 of 1985 and to examine the process server of summons of that suit in order to prove that summons was duly served on the present plaintiffs. It appears further that both the courts only on the basis of writ deed of delivery of possession exhibit-J held that the plaintiff of Title Suit No.16 of 1985 (defendant No.13 of the present suit) got possession of the suit and held that the present plaintiffs as defendants of that suit had knowledge of Title Suit No.16 of 1985. The established principle of law is that no other knowledge of a suit will be sufficient for a party unless summons of that particular suit is served as per law on the party to consists knowledge of a suit, reference may be given to the case of Md. Insal Ali Vs. Mr. Abdus Salam reported in 40 DLR(AD)193 and another case of Abdur Rashid and another Vs. Abdul Barik and another reported in 94 BLD(AD)page 83. In view of those decisions, I am of the opinion that both the courts below committed error in law occasioning failure of justice in holding that the present plaintiffs were aware about the proceeding of Title Suit No.16 of 1985 and consequently those findings are not sustainable in law. Regarding the findings by both the courts the exhibit 1 and exhibit 5 and 5(ka) being registered on the same date on Title passed to the predecessor of the present plaintiffs and saham praying defendants inasmuch as according to the courts below Ayesha Khatun having got the settlement vide registered deed dated 07.11.1945 (Exhibit-1) cannot transfer her title to the predecessors of the plaintiffs and saham praying defendants on the same date on 07.11.1945 by exhibit 5 and 5(ka). The case of the present plaintiffs is that exhibit-1 was executed on 30th Asshin, 1352 B.S. corresponding to 13/14th October, 1945 and the other two deeds exhibit 5 and 5(Ka) were executed on 03.11.1945 and the registered on 07.11.1945 so the date of execution of exhibit 1 being 14.10.1945 and the date of execution of exhibit 5 and 5(ka) being 03.11.1945 and all the three deeds having been registered on 07.11.1945 there is no legal difficulty or bar in transferring title by exhibit 5 and 5(1) to the predecessors of the plaintiffs and to the predecessor of the saham praying defendants. So in my opinion, both the courts failed to consider this aspect of the case and consequently committed error occasioning failure of justice in dismissing the suit."

<u>7. We have perused the leave petition and heard the learned Advocate. It appears that the High Court Division has found that the concern process server not being examined the proper service of summons of Title Suit No.16 of 1985 could not be proved and the courts below failed to take notice of the same and accordingly there was no proper proof of service of summons upon the plaintiffs of the Title Suit No.16 of 1985 and that the transfer made through exhibit-5 and 5(1) was found to be valid and therefore the suit dismissed by the Courts below were not proper and accordingly the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, in the facts and circumstances, calls for no interference. Furthermore the parties are not prejudiced by the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, since they can place their respective cases before the Court below.</u>

8. Accordingly the leave petitions are dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider, J: In this Rule, one of the added defendants as petitioner challenged judgment and decree dated 24.6.2002, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Chuadanga in Title Appeal No. 82 of 2001 affirming those dated 20.9.2001 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, in charge, Sadar Court, Chuadanga in Title Suit No. 62 of 1985.

2. Facts briefly stated are that the opposite party No. 1, the Head Master of Alamdanga Pilot High School, on 12.5.1985 instituted Title Suit No. 62 of 1983 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Chuadanga Sadar, Chuadanga for declaration that the resolution taken by the defendant Nos. 1 to 4, the members of the Managing Committee of Alamdanga Pilot High School, on 4.5.1985 is collusive, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. Subsequently, others including the school, represented by the Chairman of the Managing Committee were also made parties and the present petitioner, one of the Assistant Teachers of the school being entrusted with the charge of Head Master, after the plaintiff was suspended on 13.5.1985 immediately after the day of the institution of the suit, was added as defendant No. 21. In pursuant to other subsequent orders, namely suspension, termination and dismissal of the plaintiff from the service, during the pendency of the suit, the plaintiff again amended his plaint and in addition to the original prayer he also prayed for declaration that the suspension order dated 13.5.1985, the decision for dismissal of the plaintiff taken in a meeting dated 13.2.1988 and subsequent thereto the order of final dismissal of the plaintiff from the service and not giving the subsistence allowances to him during the period of suspension are illegal, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff. At the time of institution of the suit the plaintiff applied for an order of temporary injunction under Order 39 Rule 1 of the Code against the defendants wherein on 25.5.1999 the defendant No. 21 appeared and on 22.7.1999 filed written objection to contest the injunction matter. From 1985 the suit continued and none of the defendants filed any written statement in the suit denying the allegations of the plaint. On 20.9.2001 the suit was fixed for peremptory hearing but none of the defendants filed hazira on that date. The plaintiff on that date filed an application for amending the plaint which was allowed and the plaintiff then filed another application for filing a fresh copy of the plaint incorporating all the amendments in a consolidated copy of plaint, the said prayer was also accepted by the court.

3. However, the suit was taken up for hearing and the learned Assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 20.9.2001 was pleased to decree the suit ex-parte and granted the relief as sought for. Against the said ex-parte decree the defendant No. 21 preferred Title Appeal No. 82 of 2001 before the learned District Judge, Chuadanga which was ultimately heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Sadar Chuadanga, who was pleased to dismiss the appeal on contest by his judgment and decree dated 24.6.2002. Against which the defendant No. 21 appellant petitioner obtained the present rule.

4. Mr. Shahid Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant petitioner, submits that the court of appeal below committed error of law in not considering that the judgment of the Court suffers from non-dissuasion of evidence adduced by the plaintiff. It is the settled principle that the plaintiff is to prove his own case and the absence of the defendant cannot give the plaintiff any benefit of not proving his case and as such the learned court of law in dismissing the appeal without considering that the learned Assistant Judge decreed the suit without discussing the evidences adduced by the plaintiff, which is contrary to the provision of law. In this respect he submits that the court should observe minimum legal requirements and must apply judicial mind to assess the validity of the plaintiff's case. Lack of such minimum requirement and non application of judicial mind by the trial court having not been considered by the learned Additional District Judge, the impugned Judgment is erroneous resulting in error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. In support of his contention Mr. Ahmed referred to the case of Bangladesh Vs. Israil Ali and others reported in 5 BSCR(19810 P-222. He next submits that the .11 courts below failed to consider that the plaintiff by amending his plaint also amended the cause of action which under the law cannot be allowed and no copy of the amended plaint was ever served upon him. Lastly, he submits that the plaintiff in the suit filed on 12.5.85 have challenged his suspension order dated 13.5.1985 which is not the final order and as

such cannot be the subject matter of a suit nor the suspension order dated 13.5.1985 can be challenged in a suit filed on 12.5.1985. Accordingly, he submits that the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned court of appeal below suffers from error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

5. On the other hand Mr. Md. Nurul Amin appearing with Mr. Fazlul Haque Chowdhury, the learned Advocates for the opposite party No. 1 submit that the trial court upon considering all material evidences on record and being satisfied with the same passed the decree. The defendants having failed to file any written statement in 16 years denying the allegations of the plaint actually proves that there is no case against the plaintiff. Moreover, the defendant No. 21 entered appearance in the suit on 25.5.1999 but neither he filed written statement nor he finally contested the same and having not cross examined the P.W., the evidence of P.W. remains uncontroverted and there being nothing contrary in record, the evidence and the documents filed by the plaintiff are found to have been proved. The learned Assistant Judge having taken notice of all such evidences on record and having considered the same observed that upon considering the plaint, the evidences both oral and documentary produced by the plaintiff, the case of the plaintiff is found to have been proven and as such the ex-parte decree has rightly been passed. He next submits that the learned judgment of the court of appeal below having affirmed the judgment of the trial court does not require to strictly follow the provision of Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code. Moreover , Rule 143 of the C.R.O. provides that "Judgment in ex-parte case shall state specifically and explicitly which of the reliefs are granted and against which of the defendants. as such there being full compliance of such rule in the judgment of the trial court, the appellate court rightly passed the impugned judgment dismissing the appeal. He then submits that the suit was filed on 12.5.1985 challenging the decision taken by the defendants No. 1 to 4 on 4.5.1985. Thereafter in about 14 years i.e. till 1999 several changes have been brought by the school authority which compelled the plaintiff to amend his plaint in accordance with the requirements and as such the suit was not filed challenging the suspension order dated 13.5.1985 of the plaintiff. Rather that is one of the amendments brought by the plaintiff in the prayer portion as he was suspended on the very next day of institution of the suit Similarly other prayers were also made as and when the school authority and the members of the Managing Committee took different decisions as regards his service. Thus the submissions of Mr. Shahid Ahmed as to filing of the suit before the suspension order was passed is not sustainable in law. Mr. Amin lastly submits that the judgment of the lower appellate court is a proper judgment of affirmance. The appellant petitioner did not raise any of these questions before the appellate court which has been raised here, rather the point raised before the Court of appeal below was simply that the defendant had no knowledge of the suit he was not aware of the date and as such the ex-parte decree passed being beyond his knowledge is liable to be set aside. In this regard Mr. Amin submits that the appellant added as defendant No. 21 by amending the plaint when he was given the charge of the office of the Head Master and he entered appearance in the suit on 25.5.1999 and after taking several adjournments he filed written objection against the application for temporary injunction and thereafter he took several adjournments from time to time in the suit which proves that he had full knowledge of the suit and accordingly the learned Additional District Judge rightly held that the defendant appellants lack of knowledge of the suit being the only point raised by the appellant has been found to be not believable., Mr. Amin relying on an Indian decision reported in AIR 1964 (ORISSA) 98 submits that in an ex-parte case, Judgments are cryptic, evidence is barely referred to and hardly elaborate discussions are made. Mrs Mrely from the fact of absence of elaborate discussion, as in contested cases, it cannot be said that the court did not apply its judicial mind and did not appreciate the issue and evidence, properly. Thus he submits that the impugned judgment does not suffer from any error of law wherein this court's interference under the revisional jurisdiction can be called for.

6. Upon hearing the learned Advocates for both the parties at length and on perusal of the revisional application along with the papers annexed thereto and the materials on records it appears that the suit has been filed in 1985 challenging a decision of the Managing Committee but subsequent to the institution of the suit the plaintiff was temporarily suspended and thereafter on various dates several orders were passed and actions were taken by the defendant school authority which prompted the plaintiff to amend the plaint accordingly and ultimately the plaint ended with several prayers including a prayer challenging the decision of his dismissal from service during the pendency of the suit. It further appears from the record that the defendant No. 21 was made a party who entered appearance in the suit on 25.5.1999 and on 22.7.1999 he filed written objection against the injunction application but surprisingly no written statement has been filed by any of the defendants for contesting the suit. Thus when the suit was fixed for hearing on 7.8.2001 no one was present on behalf of the defendants to take step in the suit and when the plaintiff was examined as P.W.1 no one cross-examined him but even then on the prayer of the defendant No. 21 the learned judge adjourned the hearing till 2.9.2001. On 2.9.2001 the defendant petitioner again prayed for adjournment when 20.9.2001 was fixed as next date of hearing of the suit. It further appears from the record that on 20.9.2001 none of the defendants took any step in the suit and when the learned Assistant Judge took up the suit for further hearing no one was found on the side of the defendants and as such the learned Judge closed the evidence of P.W. as no one was there to cross examine the P.W. and then upon hearing the arguments of the learned advocate for the plaintiff and being satisfied with the same he decreed the suit ex-parte.

7. From the memorandum of appeal it appears that the defendant appellant did not take any ground other than the ground of lack of his knowledge and did not agitate or raise any other point before the lower appellate court. He rather concentrated on the non-search of notice, non service of fresh copy of the plaint and practicing fraud upon the court. The appellant specifically tried to make out a case that he came to know about the ex-parte decree on 25.9.2001 and as such he preferred the appeal upon obtaining the certified copy of the impugned judgment. It appears that the learned Additional District Judge found that the appellant did not come with clean hands rather by suppressing the facts and by misleading the court he tried to get a decree in the appeal. From the impugned judgment it further appears that the learned Judge held that the appellant being a school teacher filed the appeal on misleading and false statements about lack of his knowledge though it is apparent from the record that he had full knowledge and had been taking steps in the suit at least from 20.5.1999 till 2.9.2001. The suit is pending since 1985 and the plaintiff is out of his service since then but none of the defendants came to contest the suit by denying or controverting the allegations made in the plaint. Though Alamdanga High School through its Managing Committee, represented by its Chairman has been made a party and the members of the Managing Committee have also been made parties but none contested the suit and excepting defendant No. 21 none has come to challenge the decree. Mr. Amin raise a question as to whether the appellant was authorized to represent the committee of the school. In reply to this question Mr. Ahmed showed a paper that the defendant No. 15 i.e. Deputy Director of Secondary and Higher Secondary Board authorized the said defendant No. 21 to represent him in the suit and no other paper could be shown by the petitioner. In the absence of the Chairman of Managing Committee, Mr. Amin submits, how Mr. Md. Nazrul Islam, an Assistant Teacher authorized by defendant No. 15, can represent the school or the Managing Committee of the school. Thus he submits that the petitioner has no authority to represent the school or its Managing Committee and thus the appeal preferred and the petition filed before the court are not maintainable. However, in reply to Mr. Amin's submissions it appears that none of this points were raised before the court of appeal below.

<u>8. Mr. Ahmed empathetically submitted that the judgment of the trial court is not a proper judgment in the eye of law as the learned Judge did not state as to why and how he was satisfied that the plaintiff has proved his case. Having gone through record it appears that the learned Assistant Judge observed as follows:</u>

<u>"আরজি ও গৃহীত জবানবন্দী এবং প্রদর্শিত কাগজাদি পর্যালোচনা করলাম। পর্যালোচনা মতে বাদীর বক্তব্য প্রমাণিত হয়। সে কারণে বাদীগণ প্রার্থীত প্রতিকার পেতে পারেন। এটাই আদালতের গৃহীত সিদ্ধান্ত।"</u>

<u>So it appears that in the absence of cross examination of the P.W. and in the absence of contrary being proved by the defendants or in the absence of any legal pleadings having been made by any of the defendants there is no case on the side of the defendants before the court. On such back drop the above finding of the trial court appears to be based on proper appreciation of the evidence and on proper application of judicial mind and as such the submissions of Mr. Ahmed has no substance. So far the BSCR case referred Mr. Ahmed is concerned it appears that the facts are quite different. In that case the ex-parte decree was passed by simply saying that the plaintiff examined, Exts are marked for, the plaintiffs case is proved and the suit is decreed ex-parte accordingly. But in the present case it appears that the trial court upon considering the plaint, evidences both oral and documentary on record and on perusal of the same came to a definite finding that the suit has been proved. In the present case it appears that the plaintiff produced the relevant documents and proved the same and the court applied its mind with reference to the pleadings and satisfied itself as to what should be the proper proof for passing a decree on the basis of the averments made in the plaint. So the requirements for passing a decree appears to be present in this suit. Thus the BSCR case is quite distinguishable from the present one. This aspect having not been raised or challenged before the court of appeal below the learned Additional District Judge did not make any comment on the same. The appellant having challenged the judgment wholly on non-service of summons and the copy of the plaint the learned judge found the case of the appellant not justified or proved and accordingly dismissed the same. From the conduct of defendant No. 21 it appears that he did not come up with clean hands. It is the case of the plaintiff that he is a victim of conspiracy of the management of the school and as he took shelter of law he was suspended immediately after the institution of the suit and ultimately was dismissed from service during the pendency of the suit and the defendant No. 21 being the sole appellant is trying to delay and frustrate the plaintiff from enjoying the fruits of the decree so that he can remain as Head Master of the school.</u>

9. Mr. Ahmed's submission as to challenging the suspension order which is subsequent to institution of the suit, I find, has no substance as it has already been stated earlier that the cause of action of the suit has not been amended rather with the developments and actions taken by the defendants, the plaint and the prayer have been amended from time to time.

10. Mr. Amin drew my attention to another fact that the defendant No. 21 also filed an application under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code to set aside the exparte decree which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 340 of 2001 and the said Miscellaneous Case has also been rejected by order No. 254 dated 18.10.2001 as stated in counter affidavit filed by the plaintiff opposite party. It further appears from the counter affidavit that the present petitioner had been taking adjournments in the suit on every occasion, on 20.9.2001 when the date was fixed for further hearing at his instance, he was sitting with his lawyer inside the court room and watching the proceeding of the suit without taking any step. Even after plaintiffs deposition was complete the learned Advocate, who also filed power on behalf of defendant Nos. 1-4 & 6-12 and 18, did not respond to the repeated calls of the court to cross examine the P.W. thereby allowed the case to be decreed ex-parte. Such facts has not been controverted by the defendant-petitioner, which proves his malafide intention and conduct.

<u>11. Considering the facts and circumstances stated above and the conduct of the defendant No. 21 petitioner, I am of the opinion that the defendant petitioner being fully aware of the suit, was trying to take advantage of his assumption of the office of the Head Master and having failed to resist the plaintiff in succeeding in his case is now trying to delay the execution of the decision of the court so that he can continue as the Head Master and this poor plaintiff being out of office since .1985 can not enjoy the fruits of the decree. It further appears that the dependent no. 21 has taken the path of falsehood and tried to mislead the court in different manners.</u>

12. Thus I am of the opinion that there is no merit in this Rule and the learned court of appeal below did not commit any error of law in passing the impugned judgment resulting error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

13. Hence, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Additional District Judge is affirmed.

Send down the lower Court records at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Salma Masud Chowdhury, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 25.3.98 passed by the District Judge, Noakhali in Family Appeal No.7 of 1998 should not be set aside or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The opposite party as plaintiff filed Family Suit No.22 of 1995 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Senbagh, Noakhali, against the petitioner and the proforma opposite parties stating inter alia that on 13.3.90 marriage was solemnized between the petitioner and the opposite party No.1 according to Muslim Shariah Law in consideration of TK.50,000/- as dower money and out of which TK. 20,000/- was fixed as prompt dower and TK.20,000/- was fixed as deferred dower and TK.10,000/- was treated as paid up to the opposite party wife and TK.600/- was fixed as maintenance allowance. Out of the wedlock a daughter was born to them and as there was maladjustment and misunderstandings between the husband and the wife, the husband, the present petitioner, divorced his wife, opposite party No.1, on 12.3.95 and subsequently the wife as plaintiff filed a suit for dower and continuous maintenance. Defendant No.1 filed a written statement denying the material allegations made against him. The suit was decreed exparte. Against the said exparte judgment and decree, the petitioner filed a Miscellaneous Case in the Court of Assistant Judge, Senbagh, Noakhali being Miscellaneous Case No.6 of 1997 for setting aside the said exparte decree which was dismissed for default. Thereafter, on 8.3.98 the petitioner preferred Family Appeal No.7 of 1998 in the Court of District Judge, Noakhali with an application for condonation of delay of 80 days. The delay was not condoned and the appeal was dismissed.

3. Being aggrieved by that, the petitioner filed this revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure before this Court and obtained the present Rule. The petitioner as per the direction of this Court deposited Tk. 40,000/- as dower money and Tk. 3400/- as maintenance allowance in the trial court.

4. Mr. Md. Nurul Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been serving in Dhaka Electric Supply Department at Tejgaon which is an essential service and so he could not manage to get leave from the authority and go to Noakhali to file the appeal in time. He further submits that on earlier occasions also, the petitioner filed hazira and was present in the Court and when the matter was taken up for hearing he went to call his engaged lawyer who was on his legs in an-other court and could not return to the Court in time as a result of which his Miscellaneous Case No.6 of 1997 was dismissed. In support of his contention he referred to Annexure-C. He next draws my attention to the exparte

judgment and decree passed in Family Suit No.22 of 1995 and submits that the learned Family Court most illegally passed the order directing the petitioner for payment of maintenance to his divorced wife continuously, and the Family Court thereby knocked down the traditional Muslim Law as to maintenance of a divorced wife prevalent lawfully and legitimately for centuries. This decision of the trial court, according to the learned lawyer appearing on behalf of the petitioner is most ill-considered and ill-conceived as it apparently failed to take into consideration not only the whole conspectus of Muslim law relating to marriage and divorce but even the various verses of the Holy Quran on divorce. In support to his contention the learned lawyer referred to the decision as taken in the case of Hefzur Rahman Versus Shamsun Nahar Begum as reported in 4 B.L.C.(AD) page 14. The learned lawyer submits that the petitioner has complied with the direction of this Court and has paid the entire dower money and the maintenance allowance to opposite party No.1. He next submits that the learned District Judge should have condoned the delay and restored the case, considering the apparent illegality committed by the trial court while passing the exparte judgment and decree which is absolutely against the decision of the Appellate Division. The learned lawyer lastly submits that the petitioner will suffer irreparable loss if the matter is not sent back on remand.

5. Mr. Abul Kalam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No.1 frankly submits that although there is apparent illegality in the ex-parte judgment and decree of the Family Court so far as it relates to the direction given to the defendant to pay the plaintiff a sum of TK. 600/- per month continuously in future, but many opportunities were given to the defendant petitioner for the redress of the same and on every occasion he failed to appear before the court in time as a result of which his Miscellaneous case filed for setting aside the exparte decree and to restore the suit for re-hearing was dismissed. He next submits that the lower appellate court has rightly rejected the prayer of the petitioner for condonation of delay as there was an admitted delay of 80 days. He further submits that the petitioner has intentionally refrained from appearing before the Court when the matter was taken up and subsequently filed the appeal before the District Judge with an application for condonation of delay only to harass the petitioner unnecessarily. The petitioner miserably failed to show any cogent ground for the delay in preferring Family Appeal case and the learned Court rightly rejected the application for condonation of delay and the appeal.

<u>6. I have perused the revisional application along with the annexures and heard the learned lawyers appearing on behalf of the petitioner and the opposite party. It appears that the suit was decreed exparte directing the present petitioner to pay TK. 40,000/- as dower money to the plaintiff and TK. 4800/- as maintenance allowance for the Iddat period and other maintenance, total amounting to TK. 46,800/-, and it was further decreed that the petitioner would pay his minor daughter a sum of TK. 600/- per month till she attains the age of puberty and that a sum of TK.600/- is to be paid to the plaintiff by the defendant, present petitioner, as maintenance allowance for the future. The petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 1997 for setting aside the exparte decree and for restoration of the suit but it was dismissed for default on two occasions and subsequently appeal was filed with an application for condonation of delay of 80 days. I find from the record that the petitioner has paid the entire dower money along with some maintenance allowance to his divorced wife as per the direction of this Court and it is also evident from Annexure-C that he filed his hazira before the Court when the Miscellaneous case was taken up for hearing on 19.11.97 (Annexure-C). It is believable that there was no negligence on his part as he was present but he could not bring his lawyer to the court on time for which the case was dismissed. The only ground taken, for condonation of delay was that the petitioner being an employee of Electricity Supply Department, the service of which is declared as essential, it was difficult for him to get leave quickly when needed, is quite cogent to me. The last portion of the judgment passed by the Family Court directing the defendant to pay continuous maintenance allowance to the plaintiff in future is apparently illegal which is against the Personal Law set up by the Muslim jurists and the judgment passed by our Appellate Division. Muslim Law does not recognise any obligation on the part of a man to maintain a wife throughout her life time whom he had divorced.</u>

7. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The delay is condoned and the District Judge, Noakhali is directed to hear the Family Appeal on merit. The order of stay granted by this Court stands vacated. Send down a copy of the judgment and order to the Court concerned.

End.

full_judgment:
Faruque Ahmed, J: This rule at the instance of the plaintiff petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite parties No. 1-2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 28.06.1998 and 02.07.1998 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Manikgonj, in Title Appeal No. 98 of 1997 reversing those dated 29.05.1997 and 3.06.1997 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Shingail, Manikganj in Title Suit No. 118 of 1983 should not be aside and or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Short facts of the case are as follows:-Late Indra Mohan Saha father of the petitioners instituted Title Suit No. 424/79 in the Court of Munsif Shingair against opposite parties No. 2-5 for specific performance of contract stating inter alia that on 21.03.1974 the father of the petitioners entered into a Bainapatra with opposite parties No. 3 and 4 for purchase of land described in the schedule of the plaint at Taka 4,000/- and paid Tk. 3,700/- to opposite parties Nos. 3 and 4 and that the plaintiff agreed to pay Taka 300/- within 3 years from the date of the Baina Patra and that the defendants opposite parties Nos. 3 and 4 would register a Kabala in favour of the father of the petitioners, that subsequently the father of the petitioners requested opposite parties Nos. 3 and 4 to accept Tk. 300/- and register the kabala but the opposite parties Nos. 3 and 4 refused to register the kabala and hence the suit for specific performance of Contract.

3. The Title Suit No. 424/79 was transferred to the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Shingair and it was renumbered as Title Suit No. 118/83.

4. On 27.02.91 opposite party No. 1 Rafique Uddin Ahmed filed an application under order 1, Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for addition of party stating that opposite parties Nos. 3 and 4 had transferred the suit land to the opposite party No. 1 by a registered kabala on 09.12.1990. So he was added as defendant No. 5 in the suit.

5. Opposite party No. 1 alone contested the Title Suit as defendant No. 5 by filing written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contenting inter alia that the suit was not maintainable in its present form, that there was defect of parties, and that the Title Suit was liable to be dismissed.

6. Both sides examined witnesses and exhibited documents at the trial and that the trial Court decreed the suit and on appeal the title Suit was remanded to the trial Court for rehearing of the matter.

7. After remand, the case was tried by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Singair who decreed the title suit without cost by Judgment and decree dated 259.05.97 and 03.06.97 respectively.

8. The added Defendant-Opposite party No.1, preferred Title Appeal No. 98/97 before the District Judge, Manikganj.

9. The Title Appeal came up for hearing before the 2nd Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Manikganj, who allowed the Title Appeal without cost by Judgment and decree dated 28.06.98 and 02.07.1998 respectively.

10. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid appellate Judgment and decree, the plaintiff petitioners obtained the present rule.

11. Mr. Md. Mostafizur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners placed the revisional application and the impugned judgment and decree and submitted that the learned trial Court on consideration of the evidence and materials on record having decreed the suit the learned appellate Court committed error in allowing the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree of the learned trial Court holding that the suit is barred by limitation. The learned Advocate further submitted that the defendants No.1 and 2 having not filed any written statement and having not deposed in the case challenging the disputed agreement the defendant opposite party (defendant No.5) only having contested the suit claiming that he is a purchaser for value of the suit land having no knowledge of the disputed contract, the learned appellate Court committed error in allowing the appeal overlooking the provision of section 27 of the Specific Relief Act as well as section 53 A of the Transfer of Property Act.

12. Mr. Md. Haroon-Ar-Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties, on the other hand, submitted that the learned appellate Court having found that the depositions of the P.Ws. 1, 2 and 3 being contradictory, the plaintiff failed to prove his case, rightly allowed the appeal setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial Court. The learned Advocate further submitted that the finding of fact being based on materials on record is final and in the absence of any misreading or non consideration of the materials evidence on record, there is little scope for interference by this Court.

13. On perusal of the judgment passed by the learned trial Court, it appears, the learned trial Court on consideration of the evidence and materials on record found that P.Ws.1, 2 and 3 corroborated each other regarding execution of the disputed deed by defendant No.1 and 2; that consideration money for the disputed agreement was paid by the plaintiff to the defendants No.1 and 2; that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 did not contest the suit, but defendant No.5 contested the suit by filing written statement; that defendant No.5 as D.W.1 admitted in his cross-examination that he purchased the suit land from defendant No.1 and 2 having full knowledge about the present suit; that there was ad-interim order of injunction restraining the defendant no. 1 and 2 from transferring the suit land. With these findings the learned trial Court decreed the suit.

14. On appeal, the learned appellate Court held that the suit is barred by limitation as the suit has been filed beyond the period of 3 years which expired on 21.03.1977; that the plaintiff could not prove his offer and refusal by the defendants regarding execution and registration of the sale deed; that the evidence of P.Ws. 1,2 and 3 is full of inconsistencies regarding execution of the bainapatra, payment of consideration money; that the purchase by the defendant No. 5 during pendency of the suit is not void. Accordingly the learned appellate Court allowed the appeal.

15. It appears, the disputed agreement was dated 21.03.1974 and it was stipulated in the said agreement that the balance money of taka 300/- out of 4,000/- should be paid within 3 years and that 3 years expired on 21.03.1977. It further appears the suit was filed on 14.08.1979 after about 2 years 5 months of the date of expiry of the period of agreement. It appears under Article 113 of the Limitation Act the period of limitation is 3 years after expiry of the stipulated period or from the date of refusal by the seller/executants of the deed of agreement. In the present case it appears, the suit has been filed after 2 years 5 months of the date of expiry of the stipulated period of 3 years which expired on 21.03.1977. So, in my opinion, the suit having been filed admittedly within 3 years of the expiry of the stipulated date, the suit is not barred by limitation, but the learned appellate Court illegally held that the suit is barred by limitation.

<u>16. In the present suit admittedly the defendant No. 1 and 2 being the owners of the suit land executed the disputed agreement dated 21.03.1974 and inspite of due service of summons on them the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 did not appear and contest the suit, but defendant No.5 having filed an application for addition of party, he was made defendant No.5 who contested the suit by filing a written statement stating that he purchased the suit land vide registered deed dated 09.12.1990 from the defendant No.1 and 2. It also appears that the defendant No.5 as D.W.1 in his cross-examination stated that he purchased the suit land from the defendant No.1 and 2 having full knowledge of the suit pending between the plaintiff and the defendant No.1 and 2. So, it can be presumed that the defendant No.5 have purchased the suit land only to create complication and deprive the plaintiff from getting the suit land and for frustrating the decree.</u>

17. Now the question is whether the defendant No.5 having purchased the suit land during pendency of the suit and the order of ad-interim injunction granted by the learned trial Court on 11.01.1987 acquired valid title in the suit land or not. The learned appellate Court held that the deed of defendant No.5 will not be affected in any way though he purchased the suit land during pendency of the suit and the order of ad-interim injunction in as much as according to the appellate Court he will rise and fall with the result of the suit.

<u>18. It appears, the learned appellate Court totally failed to apply the correct provision of law as has been provided under Section 27 of the Specific Relief Act wherein, it has been provided that specific performance of contract can be enforced against the parties of the agreement and that any other person claiming under him by a title having arisen subsequent to the contract, except the transferees for value who purchased the suit land in good faith and without notice of the original contract for sale. In the present case, it appears, the defendant No.5 as D.W.1 admitted that he purchased the suit land having full knowledge of the suit between the plaintiff and the defendant No.1 and 2. It may be noted that the present suit is a suit for Specific Performance of Contract on the basis of the agreement dated 21.03.1974 between the plaintiff and the defendant No.1 and 2. So, the defendant No.5 having full knowledge of the said agreement as well as the pendency of the suit having purchased the suit land, in my opinion, the suit is maintainable against the defendant No. 5 also and that the suit if is decree the defendant No. 5 also will be equally bound by the decree.</u>

<u>19. It appears the learned appellate Court came to the finding that the deposition of the P.Ws.1, 2 and 3 are full of inconsistencies overlooking the fact that the agreement between the plaintiff No.1 and the defendant No.1 and 2 has not been denied by any of the defendants including defendant No.5. Since the disputed agreement has not been denied by any of the defendants it can be said that the said agreement has been admitted by the defendants and the admitted fact as per provision of law need not be proved. So inspite of the fact that the appellate Court found some inconsistencies in the depositions of the P.Ws, I am of the opinion, that since the disputed agreement has not been denied by any of the defendants the inconsistencies if any in the deposition of the P.Ws it will be not a bar for getting a decree in the present suit by the plaintiff.</u>

20. Thus, for the aforesaid reasons and discussions I am of the opinion that the learned appellate Court committed error occasioning failure of justice in allowing the appeal by the impugned judgment and decree calling for interference by this Court.

21. Accordingly, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs and the judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate Court are set aside and those of the learned trial Court decreeing the suit are maintained.

22. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby vacated.

23. Send down the L.C. Records immediately.

End.
